var ENT_SAMPLE=SAMPLE_CLEAN; // default shown in the editor function labClasses(cls){return cls==='err'?'err':(cls==='info'?'info':(cls==='diag'?'diag':'out'));} // ---- Linux+ Script Validator samples ---- var LSAMPLE_CLEAN=[ '# Linux sample (CLEAN): create an app user, install & enable a service, open the firewall', '# Every line is valid \u2014 this should validate with 0 errors.', 'sudo useradd -m -s /bin/bash appuser', 'sudo usermod -aG sudo appuser', 'sudo dnf install -y nginx', 'sudo systemctl enable nginx', 'sudo systemctl start nginx', 'systemctl is-enabled nginx', 'sudo firewall-cmd --add-service=http --permanent', 'sudo firewall-cmd --reload', 'mkdir -p /home/appuser/site', 'chmod 755 /home/appuser/site' ].join('\n'); var LSAMPLE_PERM=[ '# Permissions & ownership \u2014 one deliberate mistake, fix shown in a comment', 'mkdir -p /srv/data', 'touch /srv/data/report.csv', '# MISTAKE: chmod 777 gives the world write access (security risk).', 'chmod 777 /srv/data/report.csv', '# CORRECT: least privilege \u2014 owner rw, group r, other none:', '# chmod 640 /srv/data/report.csv', '# MISTAKE: chown needs root; without sudo it is denied.', 'chown appuser:appuser /srv/data/report.csv', '# CORRECT: sudo chown appuser:appuser /srv/data/report.csv', 'ls -l /srv/data' ].join('\n'); var LSAMPLE_SVC=[ '# Services, packages & group mistakes to practice fixing (fixes in comments)', '# MISTAKE 1: apt subcommand typo.', 'sudo apt instal nginx', '# CORRECT: sudo apt install nginx', '# MISTAKE 2: managing a service without sudo.', 'systemctl restart sshd', '# CORRECT: sudo systemctl restart sshd', '# MISTAKE 3: starting a unit that is not installed.', 'sudo systemctl start doesnotexist', '# CORRECT: install the package first, then start the real unit name.', '# MISTAKE 4: usermod -G without -a drops existing groups.', 'sudo usermod -G docker appuser', '# CORRECT: sudo usermod -aG docker appuser' ].join('\n'); var LSAMPLES=[ {id:'clean', name:'Clean provisioning script', desc:'User + service + firewall \u2014 validates with 0 errors', text:LSAMPLE_CLEAN}, {id:'perm', name:'Permissions mistakes', desc:'chmod 777 + missing sudo \u2014 fixes shown in comments', text:LSAMPLE_PERM}, {id:'svc', name:'Service & package mistakes', desc:'Four common admin mistakes to practice fixing', text:LSAMPLE_SVC} ]; // ---- SecurityX Tooling Validator samples ---- var SECX_ENT=[ '# SecurityX sample (CLEAN): stand up a TLS key + CSR, verify a peer, hash an artifact', '# Every line is valid \u2014 this should validate with 0 errors.', 'openssl genpkey -algorithm RSA -pkeyopt rsa_keygen_bits:3072 -out server.key', 'openssl req -new -key server.key -out server.csr -subj "/CN=app.example.com/O=Example"', 'openssl s_client -connect example.com:443 -servername example.com', 'openssl verify -CAfile ca.crt server.crt', 'sha256sum installer.bin', 'nmap -sV -p- 10.0.0.0/24', 'syft nginx:latest -o spdx-json=sbom.json', 'trivy image nginx:latest' ].join('\n'); var SECX_CRYPTO=[ '# Crypto / PKI \u2014 one deliberate mistake, fix shown in a comment', 'openssl genpkey -algorithm ED25519 -out id_ed25519.key', '# MISTAKE: -aes-256-cbc with no KDF is weak and lacks integrity.', 'openssl enc -aes-256-cbc -in secret.txt -out secret.enc', '# CORRECT (AEAD + strong KDF):', '# openssl enc -aes-256-gcm -pbkdf2 -iter 600000 -salt -in secret.txt -out secret.enc', '# MISTAKE: DSA keys are deprecated and rejected.', 'ssh-keygen -t dsa -f id_dsa', '# CORRECT: ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "analyst@corp"' ].join('\n'); var SECX_DETECT=[ '# Detection & IR mistakes to practice fixing (fixes in comments)', '# MISTAKE 1: yara needs BOTH a rule file and a target.', 'yara rules.yar', '# CORRECT: yara rules.yar /path/to/sample', '# MISTAKE 2: oscap eval without a profile.', 'oscap xccdf eval ssg-rhel9-ds.xml', '# CORRECT: oscap xccdf eval --profile cis --report r.html ssg-rhel9-ds.xml', '# MISTAKE 3: gpg encrypt with no recipient.', 'gpg --encrypt report.pdf', '# CORRECT: gpg --encrypt -r ir@example.com report.pdf', 'curl -s "https://services.nvd.nist.gov/rest/json/cves/2.0?cveId=CVE-2024-3094"' ].join('\n'); var SECX_INLINE=[ {id:'clean', name:'Clean PKI + scan flow', desc:'Key/CSR, TLS verify, SBOM + scan \u2014 validates with 0 errors', text:SECX_ENT}, {id:'crypto', name:'Crypto mistakes', desc:'Weak cipher + deprecated key \u2014 fixes shown in comments', text:SECX_CRYPTO}, {id:'detect', name:'Detection & IR mistakes', desc:'yara/oscap/gpg invocation errors to practice fixing', text:SECX_DETECT} ]; // ---- ITIL 5 / Atlassian JSM CLI Validator samples ---- var ITIL_ENT=[ '# ITIL 5 / JSM sample (CLEAN): authenticate, raise an incident, work it, resolve it', '# Every line is a valid acli / jsm invocation \u2014 this should validate with 0 errors.', 'acli jira auth login --web', 'acli jira workitem create --project ITSM --type Incident --summary "Checkout page returning 500 errors" --assignee @me --label "payments,p1"', 'acli jira workitem transition --key ITSM-14 --status "In Progress"', 'acli jira workitem comment create --key ITSM-14 --body "Root cause identified; fix rolling out."', 'jql "project = ITSM AND type = Incident AND statusCategory != Done ORDER BY priority DESC"', 'jsm sla show ITSM-14', 'acli jira workitem transition --key ITSM-14 --status Resolved' ].join('\n'); var ITIL_CHANGE=[ '# Change Enablement \u2014 one deliberate mistake, fix shown in a comment', 'acli jira workitem create --project ITSM --type Change --summary "Upgrade payment gateway to v4" --label "normal-change"', '# MISTAKE: a normal change must be authorised before scheduling.', 'acli jira workitem transition --key ITSM-16 --status "Scheduled"', '# CORRECT (route to CAB first, then approve):', '# acli jira workitem transition --key ITSM-16 --status "Awaiting CAB"', '# jsm approval approve ITSM-16' ].join('\n'); var ITIL_API=[ '# REST API / automation mistakes to practice fixing (fixes in comments)', '# MISTAKE 1: Atlassian Cloud basic auth needs an API token, not your password.', 'curl -s -u me@acme.com:hunter2 https://acme.atlassian.net/rest/servicedeskapi/request/ITSM-14/sla', '# CORRECT: curl -s -u me@acme.com:$TOKEN https://acme.atlassian.net/rest/servicedeskapi/request/ITSM-14/sla', '# MISTAKE 2: creating an issue needs a nested fields object.', 'curl -X POST --data \'{"summary":"API incident"}\' https://acme.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issue', '# CORRECT: --data \'{"fields":{"project":{"key":"ITSM"},"issuetype":{"name":"Incident"},"summary":"API incident"}}\'', 'acli jira workitem search --jql "project = ITSM AND created >= -7d"' ].join('\n'); var ITIL_INLINE=[ {id:'clean', name:'Clean incident lifecycle', desc:'Auth \u2192 raise \u2192 work \u2192 resolve \u2014 validates with 0 errors', text:ITIL_ENT}, {id:'change', name:'Change Enablement mistake', desc:'Skipping CAB authorisation \u2014 fix shown in comments', text:ITIL_CHANGE}, {id:'api', name:'REST API mistakes', desc:'Token auth + fields-object errors to practice fixing', text:ITIL_API} ]; // ---- CCNP dedicated Script Validator quick-pick samples ---- var SAMPLE_CCNP_CLEAN = "! CCNP sample (CLEAN): multi-area OSPF core + HSRP gateway + L3 EtherChannel\n! Every line is valid \u2014 this should validate with 0 errors.\nenable\nconfigure terminal\nrouter ospf 1\n router-id 2.2.2.2\n network 10.1.0.0 0.0.255.255 area 0\n network 10.2.0.0 0.0.255.255 area 1\nexit\ninterface range gi0/1 - 2\n no switchport\n channel-group 1 mode active\nexit\ninterface port-channel 1\n ip address 10.0.0.1 255.255.255.252\nexit\ninterface vlan 10\n ip address 10.10.10.2 255.255.255.0\n standby 1 ip 10.10.10.1\n standby 1 priority 110\n standby 1 preempt\nend\nshow ip ospf neighbor"; var SAMPLE_CCNP_MISTAKE = "! CCNP sample: four common mistakes to practice fixing (fixes in comments)\nrouter eigrp 100\n network 10.0.0.0 255.0.0.0\n! MISTAKE 1: EIGRP 'network' needs a WILDCARD mask, not a subnet mask.\n! CORRECT: network 10.0.0.0 0.255.255.255\nexit\nrouter ospf 1\n redistribute eigrp 100 subnets\n! MISTAKE 2: redistributing INTO ospf from eigrp needs no eigrp-side metric,\n! but redistributing eigrp FROM ospf does need a full seed metric - shown here reversed on purpose.\nexit\ninterface vlan 20\n standby 2 ip 10.20.20.1\n standby 2 priority 150\n! MISTAKE 3: priority alone doesn't reclaim active status after recovery.\n! CORRECT: standby 2 preempt\nexit\nroute-map SET_LP permit 10\n set local-preference 200\nexit\nrouter bgp 65001\n neighbor 203.0.113.2 route-map SET_LP out\n! MISTAKE 4: local-preference only matters on routes coming IN to the AS.\n! CORRECT: neighbor 203.0.113.2 route-map SET_LP in\nend"; var SAMPLES_CCNP = [ {id:'clean', name:'Clean ENCOR core config', desc:'Multi-area OSPF, HSRP gateway, L3 EtherChannel \u2014 validates with 0 errors', text:SAMPLE_CCNP_CLEAN}, {id:'mistake', name:'Common CCNP mistakes', desc:'EIGRP wildcard mask, redistribution metric, HSRP preempt, BGP route-map direction', text:SAMPLE_CCNP_MISTAKE} ]; // ---- CCIE dedicated Script Validator quick-pick samples ---- var SAMPLE_CCIE_CLEAN = "! CCIE sample (CLEAN): MPLS L3VPN PE with a customer VRF and MP-BGP VPNv4\n! Every line is valid \u2014 this should validate with 0 errors.\nenable\nconfigure terminal\nvrf definition CUST_A\n rd 65000:1\n address-family ipv4\n route-target export 65000:1\n route-target import 65000:1\nexit\ninterface gi0/1\n vrf forwarding CUST_A\n ip address 10.1.1.1 255.255.255.252\n no shutdown\nexit\nrouter bgp 65000\n neighbor 2.2.2.2 remote-as 65000\n neighbor 2.2.2.2 update-source Loopback0\n address-family vpnv4\n neighbor 2.2.2.2 activate\n neighbor 2.2.2.2 send-community extended\nend\nshow vrf"; var SAMPLE_CCIE_MISTAKE = "! CCIE sample: four common mistakes to practice fixing (fixes in comments)\nvrf definition CUST_B\n rd 65000:2\n address-family ipv4\n route-target export 65000:2\n route-target import 65000:3\n! MISTAKE 1: import/export route-targets don't match across sites \u2014 routes never leak in.\n! CORRECT: both sides import/export the SAME route-target (e.g. 65000:2).\nexit\nrouter bgp 65000\n neighbor 3.3.3.3 remote-as 65000\n address-family vpnv4\n neighbor 3.3.3.3 activate\n! MISTAKE 2: forgot 'send-community extended' \u2014 route-targets get stripped in transit.\n! CORRECT: neighbor 3.3.3.3 send-community extended\nexit\ninterface Tunnel0\n tunnel mode gre multipoint\n ip nhrp network-id 1\n! MISTAKE 3: a DMVPN spoke needs 'ip nhrp nhs ' to register.\n! CORRECT: ip nhrp nhs 172.16.0.1\nexit\ncrypto ikev2 proposal PROP\n encryption aes-cbc-256\n integrity sha256\n group 14\n! MISTAKE 4: the peer's proposal (elsewhere) offers aes-cbc-128 \u2014 no overlap, IKE never negotiates.\n! CORRECT: include a proposal that matches an algorithm the peer actually offers.\nend"; var SAMPLES_CCIE = [ {id:'clean', name:'Clean MPLS L3VPN PE config', desc:'VRF, PE-CE interface, MP-BGP VPNv4 \u2014 validates with 0 errors', text:SAMPLE_CCIE_CLEAN}, {id:'mistake', name:'Common CCIE mistakes', desc:'RT mismatch, missing send-community, DMVPN NHS, IKEv2 proposal mismatch', text:SAMPLE_CCIE_MISTAKE} ]; window.SCRIPT_SAMPLES_AZ802 = [{"id":1,"title":"Promote a server to a domain controller","level":"CORE","cat":"AD DS - Domain Controllers","purpose":"Install the AD DS role and promote the server into an existing domain, placing it in the correct site.","config":["# Install the role and its management tools","Install-WindowsFeature AD-Domain-Services -IncludeManagementTools","","# Promote into an existing domain","Install-ADDSDomainController `"," -DomainName 'corp.contoso.com' `"," -Credential (Get-Credential) `"," -SiteName 'London' `"," -InstallDns:$true `"," -DatabasePath 'E:\\NTDS' -LogPath 'E:\\NTDS' -SysvolPath 'E:\\SYSVOL' `"," -NoGlobalCatalog:$false -Force","","# Verify after reboot","Get-ADDomainController -Filter * |"," Select-Object Name,Site,IsGlobalCatalog,IsReadOnly,OperatingSystem"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: Install-WindowsFeature adds the binaries; Install-ADDSDomainController performs the promotion. -SiteName places the DC in the right AD site so clients authenticate locally, and explicit -DatabasePath / -LogPath / -SysvolPath keep the database off the system volume. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Omitting -SiteName drops the DC into Default-First-Site-Name, so clients across the WAN may authenticate against it. On an Azure VM, leaving the paths at their defaults can place NTDS.dit on the temporary disk, which is destroyed on deallocation. WHY IT MATTERS: Domain controller deployment is core to the largest AZ-802 domain, and the disk-placement detail is specifically tested for Azure-hosted DCs."},{"id":2,"title":"Deploy a read-only domain controller for a branch office","level":"INTER","cat":"AD DS - Domain Controllers","purpose":"Promote an RODC and scope which accounts may have their passwords cached on it.","config":["Install-WindowsFeature AD-Domain-Services -IncludeManagementTools","","Install-ADDSDomainController `"," -DomainName 'corp.contoso.com' -Credential (Get-Credential) `"," -SiteName 'Branch-Leeds' -ReadOnlyReplica:$true `"," -DelegatedAdministratorAccountName 'CORP\\Branch-Admins' `"," -InstallDns:$true -Force","","# Allow only branch accounts to cache passwords here","Add-ADDomainControllerPasswordReplicationPolicy -Identity DC03 `"," -AllowedList 'Branch-Users','Branch-Computers'","","# Review what has actually been cached","Get-ADDomainControllerPasswordReplicationPolicyUsage -Identity DC03 -RevealedAccounts"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: -ReadOnlyReplica creates an RODC that holds a read-only copy and replicates one way only. The Password Replication Policy allow-list limits which credentials are ever cached locally, so a stolen server yields almost nothing. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Adding privileged groups to the allowed list defeats the purpose entirely — administrator credentials would then be cached on a physically insecure machine. The denied list protects those groups by default and should not be weakened. WHY IT MATTERS: RODCs appear regularly in AZ-802 scenarios about branch offices and physical security, and the PRP allow/deny distinction is the detail being tested."},{"id":3,"title":"Find, transfer, and seize FSMO roles","level":"CORE","cat":"AD DS - FSMO","purpose":"Locate all five operations master roles, move them gracefully, and seize them when a holder is gone for good.","config":["# Forest-wide roles","Get-ADForest | Select-Object SchemaMaster,DomainNamingMaster","","# Domain-wide roles","Get-ADDomain | Select-Object PDCEmulator,RIDMaster,InfrastructureMaster","","# Graceful transfer - the current holder is online and agrees","Move-ADDirectoryServerOperationMasterRole -Identity DC02 `"," -OperationMasterRole PDCEmulator,RIDMaster,InfrastructureMaster","","# Seizure - ONLY when the holder will never return","Move-ADDirectoryServerOperationMasterRole -Identity DC02 `"," -OperationMasterRole SchemaMaster,DomainNamingMaster -Force"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: Move-ADDirectoryServerOperationMasterRole handles both operations: without -Force it negotiates a graceful transfer, and with -Force it seizes the role unilaterally. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Seizing a role and then bringing the original holder back online leaves two DCs claiming the same role, which corrupts the directory. A seized holder must be forcibly demoted and its metadata cleaned before it ever rejoins. WHY IT MATTERS: FSMO transfer versus seizure is one of the most reliably tested AD DS distinctions on AZ-802."},{"id":4,"title":"Create a group managed service account","level":"INTER","cat":"AD DS - Service Accounts","purpose":"Create the KDS root key and a gMSA whose password Active Directory rotates automatically.","config":["# Once per forest - creates the Key Distribution Service root key","Add-KdsRootKey -EffectiveImmediately","","# In a lab only, bypass the 10-hour replication wait:","# Add-KdsRootKey -EffectiveTime ((Get-Date).AddHours(-10))","","New-ADServiceAccount -Name 'gMSA-SQL' `"," -DNSHostName 'gMSA-SQL.corp.contoso.com' `"," -PrincipalsAllowedToRetrieveManagedPassword 'SQL-Servers'","","# On each member server that will use it","Install-ADServiceAccount -Identity 'gMSA-SQL'","Test-ADServiceAccount -Identity 'gMSA-SQL'"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: The KDS root key lets AD generate and rotate the 240-character password. PrincipalsAllowedToRetrieveManagedPassword names the computers permitted to fetch it, so several servers in a farm can share one identity. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Creating the gMSA before the KDS root key is effective fails. By default the key becomes usable ten hours after creation to allow for replication — -EffectiveImmediately does not actually bypass that in a multi-DC forest. WHY IT MATTERS: gMSAs remove stored service-account passwords entirely, and the KDS root key prerequisite is a specific tested detail."},{"id":5,"title":"Bulk-create users from a CSV with AGDLP group nesting","level":"CORE","cat":"AD DS - Users and Groups","purpose":"Create accounts from a spreadsheet and place them into the correct global and domain local groups.","config":["# Global group holds accounts; domain local group holds permissions","New-ADGroup -Name 'GG-Finance' -GroupScope Global -GroupCategory Security `"," -Path 'OU=Groups,DC=corp,DC=contoso,DC=com'","New-ADGroup -Name 'DL-FinanceShare-Modify' -GroupScope DomainLocal `"," -GroupCategory Security -Path 'OU=Groups,DC=corp,DC=contoso,DC=com'","Add-ADGroupMember -Identity 'DL-FinanceShare-Modify' -Members 'GG-Finance'","","# newstaff.csv: Name,Sam,Department,Pw","Import-Csv .\\newstaff.csv | ForEach-Object {"," New-ADUser -Name $_.Name -SamAccountName $_.Sam `"," -UserPrincipalName \"$($_.Sam)@corp.contoso.com\" `"," -Department $_.Department `"," -Path 'OU=Staff,DC=corp,DC=contoso,DC=com' `"," -AccountPassword (ConvertTo-SecureString $_.Pw -AsPlainText -Force) `"," -ChangePasswordAtLogon $true -Enabled $true"," Add-ADGroupMember -Identity 'GG-Finance' -Members $_.Sam","}"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: AGDLP puts Accounts into Global groups, those into Domain Local groups, and assigns Permissions to the domain local group. Import-Csv plus ForEach-Object turns a spreadsheet into accounts without touching the GUI. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Assigning permissions directly to a global group works in a single domain but breaks the model across a forest, because a global group can only contain principals from its own domain. WHY IT MATTERS: Bulk account creation and group strategy both appear in AZ-802, and PowerShell syntax is tested literally rather than conceptually."},{"id":6,"title":"Audit replication health across every domain controller","level":"INTER","cat":"AD DS - Replication","purpose":"Produce a summary of replication state and drill into any DC reporting failures.","config":["# Fastest overall picture","repadmin /replsummary","","# Detail for one failing DC","repadmin /showrepl DC03 /errorsonly","","# The PowerShell equivalent","Get-ADReplicationFailure -Target DC03 |"," Select-Object Server,FirstFailureTime,FailureCount,LastError","","Get-ADReplicationPartnerMetadata -Target * -Partition * |"," Select-Object Server,Partner,LastReplicationSuccess,LastReplicationResult |"," Where-Object LastReplicationResult -ne 0","","# Force replication once the cause is fixed","repadmin /syncall DC03 /AdeP"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: repadmin /replsummary aggregates every source and destination pair into one table with a failure percentage, so a broken partner is obvious. Get-ADReplicationFailure gives the same information as objects you can filter and export. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Running repadmin /syncall before fixing the underlying cause simply repeats the failure. The error code in the summary — 8524 for DNS, 5 for access denied, 1722 for RPC — tells you what to fix first. WHY IT MATTERS: Replication troubleshooting is explicitly listed in the AZ-802 troubleshooting domain and is one of the heaviest reported topics."},{"id":7,"title":"Restore a deleted object from the Active Directory Recycle Bin","level":"CORE","cat":"AD DS - Recovery","purpose":"Enable the Recycle Bin and restore a deleted user with all attributes and group memberships intact.","config":["# One-time, forest-wide, and irreversible","Enable-ADOptionalFeature -Identity 'Recycle Bin Feature' `"," -Scope ForestOrConfigurationSet -Target 'corp.contoso.com'","","# Find the deleted object","Get-ADObject -Filter { displayName -eq 'Priya Nair' } -IncludeDeletedObjects |"," Select-Object Name,ObjectClass,Deleted,LastKnownParent","","# Restore it","Get-ADObject -Filter { displayName -eq 'Priya Nair' } -IncludeDeletedObjects |"," Restore-ADObject","","# Restore an entire OU: parent first, then children","Get-ADObject -Filter { lastKnownParent -eq 'OU=Finance,DC=corp,DC=contoso,DC=com' } `"," -IncludeDeletedObjects | Restore-ADObject"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: With the Recycle Bin enabled, a deleted object retains every attribute and group membership for the deleted-object lifetime, so Restore-ADObject returns it fully intact. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Without the Recycle Bin the object becomes a tombstone with most attributes stripped, and recovery requires an authoritative restore from backup. The feature does not help retroactively for objects deleted before it was enabled. WHY IT MATTERS: Object recovery is explicitly in the AZ-802 troubleshooting objectives and is reported as appearing on the live exam."},{"id":8,"title":"Perform an authoritative restore with ntdsutil","level":"ADV","cat":"AD DS - Recovery","purpose":"Recover deliberately deleted objects when the Recycle Bin was never enabled.","config":["# Boot into Directory Services Restore Mode","bcdedit /set safeboot dsrepair","Restart-Computer","","# Restore system state from backup, then before rebooting:","ntdsutil"," activate instance ntds"," authoritative restore"," restore subtree \"OU=Finance,DC=corp,DC=contoso,DC=com\""," quit"," quit","","# Return to normal boot","bcdedit /deletevalue safeboot","Restart-Computer"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: An authoritative restore increments the version numbers on the restored objects so they win replication conflicts and propagate outward to every other domain controller. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: A non-authoritative restore brings the DC back and then lets normal replication overwrite it with current data — which immediately re-deletes the objects you were trying to recover. WHY IT MATTERS: The authoritative versus non-authoritative distinction is directly testable and is listed under recovering the AD database using DSRM."},{"id":9,"title":"Repair SYSVOL replication on a domain controller","level":"ADV","cat":"AD DS - Recovery","purpose":"Force a non-authoritative DFSR sync of SYSVOL on a DC that is not sharing it.","config":["# Confirm the DC is not sharing SYSVOL","Get-WinEvent -LogName 'DFS Replication' -MaxEvents 20 |"," Where-Object Id -in 4602,4614,4604 |"," Select-Object TimeCreated,Id,Message","","# Non-authoritative sync: set msDFSR-Enabled FALSE, restart, then TRUE","$dn = 'CN=SYSVOL Subscription,CN=Domain System Volume,' +"," 'CN=DFSR-LocalSettings,CN=DC02,OU=Domain Controllers,DC=corp,DC=contoso,DC=com'","Set-ADObject -Identity $dn -Replace @{ 'msDFSR-Enabled' = $false }","Restart-Service DFSR","","Set-ADObject -Identity $dn -Replace @{ 'msDFSR-Enabled' = $true }","Restart-Service DFSR","","# Event 4602 confirms SYSVOL is shared again"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: Toggling msDFSR-Enabled off and on forces DFSR to discard its local SYSVOL copy and re-seed from a healthy partner, which is the supported non-authoritative recovery. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Restarting the DFSR service without toggling the attribute changes nothing — the replication group state is what is stuck, not the service. Event 4614 means it is still waiting for initial sync, not that it succeeded. WHY IT MATTERS: SYSVOL recovery is named explicitly in the AZ-802 objectives, and event 4602 versus 4614 is the practical success signal."},{"id":10,"title":"Create, link, and scope a Group Policy Object","level":"CORE","cat":"Group Policy","purpose":"Build a GPO, link it to an OU, and restrict it to one security group without breaking retrieval.","config":["New-GPO -Name 'Baseline - Workstations' -Comment 'Security baseline'","","New-GPLink -Name 'Baseline - Workstations' `"," -Target 'OU=Workstations,DC=corp,DC=contoso,DC=com' `"," -LinkEnabled Yes -Order 1","","# Security filtering: remove the default, add the target group","Set-GPPermission -Name 'Baseline - Workstations' `"," -TargetName 'Authenticated Users' -TargetType Group -PermissionLevel None","Set-GPPermission -Name 'Baseline - Workstations' `"," -TargetName 'GG-Finance-Workstations' -TargetType Group -PermissionLevel GpoApply","","# Restore Read for computer accounts so the GPO can still be retrieved","Set-GPPermission -Name 'Baseline - Workstations' `"," -TargetName 'Domain Computers' -TargetType Group -PermissionLevel GpoRead"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: GpoApply grants both Read and Apply Group Policy to the target group. Restoring GpoRead for Domain Computers satisfies the authenticated-read requirement introduced by a security update. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Removing Authenticated Users without granting Read to Domain Computers means the GPO cannot be retrieved at all, and it silently stops applying to everyone — a very common and confusing failure. WHY IT MATTERS: Group Policy is reported as one of the heaviest AZ-802 areas, and this specific security-filtering gotcha is a real-world trap."},{"id":11,"title":"Report which GPOs actually applied and why","level":"CORE","cat":"Group Policy","purpose":"Use Group Policy Results to find the winning GPO and the reason others were filtered out.","config":["# Quick console summary","gpresult /r /scope:computer","","# Full HTML report - shows every setting and which GPO supplied it","gpresult /h C:\\Temp\\report.html /f","","# Remote, via PowerShell","Get-GPResultantSetOfPolicy -Computer SRV01 -User CORP\\pnair `"," -ReportType Html -Path C:\\Temp\\rsop.html","","# Check inheritance and precedence on the OU","Get-GPInheritance -Target 'OU=Finance,DC=corp,DC=contoso,DC=com' |"," Select-Object -ExpandProperty InheritedGpoLinks |"," Select-Object DisplayName,Enforced,Enabled"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: Group Policy Results reports what actually applied on a live machine, including a Denied (Security) or Denied (WMI Filter) reason for each GPO that did not. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Group Policy Modeling answers a different question — it simulates a hypothetical user and computer combination rather than reporting reality. Using Modeling to diagnose a live problem gives you the theoretical answer, not the actual one. WHY IT MATTERS: Modeling versus Results is directly tested, and candidates report both appearing on the live exam."},{"id":12,"title":"Simulate a Group Policy change before deploying it","level":"INTER","cat":"Group Policy","purpose":"Use Group Policy Modeling to predict the effect of a proposed link or membership change.","config":["# Simulate: what would apply to this user on this computer?","Get-GPResultantSetOfPolicy -ReportType Html -Path C:\\Temp\\model.html","","# Targeted simulation against specific containers","Import-Module GroupPolicy","$params = @{"," User = 'CORP\\pnair'"," Computer = 'CORP\\WKS-4412'"," ReportType = 'Xml'"," Path = 'C:\\Temp\\model.xml'","}","Get-GPResultantSetOfPolicy @params","","# Inspect the resulting XML for the winning settings","[xml]$rsop = Get-Content C:\\Temp\\model.xml","$rsop.Rsop.ComputerResults.GPO | Select-Object Name,Enabled,IsValid"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: Modeling runs the policy engine against a hypothetical combination without touching the target machine, so you see the outcome before committing a change. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Modeling cannot account for WMI filters that depend on live hardware state, so a filter such as a manufacturer or model check may evaluate differently in reality than in the simulation. WHY IT MATTERS: Testing a change before deployment is a recurring AZ-802 scenario shape, and Modeling is the intended answer."},{"id":13,"title":"Map a network drive with Group Policy Preferences and item-level targeting","level":"CORE","cat":"Group Policy","purpose":"Deliver a departmental drive mapping to only the members of one security group.","config":["# GPMC path:","# User Configuration > Preferences > Windows Settings > Drive Maps","#","# Action ............. Update","# Location ........... \\\\fileserver\\finance","# Reconnect .......... Enabled","# Drive Letter ....... F:","# Label .............. Finance","# Item-level targeting: Security Group = CORP\\GG-Finance","","# Confirm the preference is present in the GPO","Get-GPRegistryValue -Name 'Drive Maps - Departmental' -Key 'HKCU\\Network' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue","Get-GPOReport -Name 'Drive Maps - Departmental' -ReportType Html -Path C:\\Temp\\drives.html"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: The Update action modifies the mapping if it exists and creates it if it does not, which is the idempotent choice. Item-level targeting scopes a single preference item to a group, so one GPO can serve every department. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Using the Replace action deletes and recreates the mapping at every refresh, which disconnects users mid-session. Using Create means later changes to the path are never applied to machines that already have the drive. WHY IT MATTERS: Drive mapping via Group Policy Preferences is reported as appearing on the live AZ-802 exam specifically."},{"id":14,"title":"Delegate GPO editing without granting Domain Admin","level":"INTER","cat":"Group Policy","purpose":"Give a desktop team the ability to edit one GPO and nothing else.","config":["Set-GPPermission -Name 'Baseline - Workstations' `"," -TargetName 'GG-DesktopAdmins' -TargetType Group -PermissionLevel GpoEdit","","# Review the full permission set on the GPO","Get-GPPermission -Name 'Baseline - Workstations' -All |"," Select-Object @{n='Who';e={$_.Trustee.Name}},Permission","","# Allow the same group to manage links on one OU only","$ou = [ADSI]'LDAP://OU=Workstations,DC=corp,DC=contoso,DC=com'","# (Delegation of Control Wizard: Manage Group Policy links)"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: GpoEdit grants edit rights on that single GPO without any ability to delete it, change its security, or touch any other policy. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Granting GpoEditDeleteModifySecurity gives the group the ability to change who else can edit the GPO, which is effectively a privilege-escalation path. WHY IT MATTERS: Delegation is listed in the AD DS security objectives, and least-privilege answers are consistently the correct ones on this exam."},{"id":15,"title":"Check and force Microsoft Entra Connect synchronisation","level":"CORE","cat":"Hybrid Identity","purpose":"Inspect the sync scheduler and trigger a delta or full cycle from the Entra Connect server.","config":["Import-Module ADSync","","Get-ADSyncScheduler | Select-Object SyncCycleEnabled,"," NextSyncCyclePolicyType,NextSyncCycleStartTimeInUTC,CurrentlyEffectiveSyncCycleInterval","","# Delta cycle - only changed objects","Start-ADSyncSyncCycle -PolicyType Delta","","# Full cycle - reprocesses every object, expensive","Start-ADSyncSyncCycle -PolicyType Initial","","# Confirm from the cloud side","Connect-MgGraph -Scopes 'Organization.Read.All'","Get-MgOrganization | Select-Object DisplayName,OnPremisesLastSyncDateTime"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: The scheduler runs a delta cycle every 30 minutes by default. Start-ADSyncSyncCycle -PolicyType Delta forces one immediately when you need a change to appear without waiting. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Running -PolicyType Initial on a large directory reprocesses every object and can take hours, during which normal synchronisation is blocked. It is not a faster version of Delta. WHY IT MATTERS: Hybrid identity troubleshooting appears in AZ-802, and the 30-minute default versus two-minute password sync is a tested detail."},{"id":16,"title":"Deploy Microsoft Entra Password Protection for on-premises AD DS","level":"ADV","cat":"Hybrid Identity","purpose":"Register the proxy and forest, then confirm the DC agents are reporting.","config":["# On a member server - install the proxy service, then register it","Import-Module AzureADPasswordProtection","Register-AzureADPasswordProtectionProxy -AccountUpn 'admin@contoso.com'","Register-AzureADPasswordProtectionForest -AccountUpn 'admin@contoso.com'","","# On each writable domain controller: install the DC agent, then reboot","","# Confirm agents are healthy and have the current policy","Get-AzureADPasswordProtectionDCAgent |"," Select-Object ServerFQDN,SoftwareVersion,HeartbeatUTC,PasswordPolicyDateUTC","","Get-AzureADPasswordProtectionProxy |"," Select-Object ServerFQDN,SoftwareVersion,HeartbeatUTC"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: The proxy relays the banned-password policy from Entra ID into the forest, and the DC agent evaluates every password change against it at the point of change. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Installing the DC agent without registering the forest leaves the agents with no policy to enforce, so weak passwords continue to be accepted silently. The agent also requires a reboot to become active. WHY IT MATTERS: Entra Password Protection for AD DS is new to the AZ-802 blueprint and is reported as appearing on the live exam."},{"id":17,"title":"Run a command against many servers at once","level":"CORE","cat":"Remote Management","purpose":"Use Invoke-Command to collect the same information from a fleet in one call.","config":["$servers = 'SRV01','SRV02','SRV03'","","Invoke-Command -ComputerName $servers -ScriptBlock {"," [pscustomobject]@{"," Name = $env:COMPUTERNAME"," Uptime = (Get-Date) - (Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem).LastBootUpTime"," FreeGB = [math]::Round((Get-PSDrive C).Free / 1GB, 1)"," W32Time = (Get-Service W32Time).Status"," }","} | Select-Object Name,Uptime,FreeGB,W32Time | Format-Table -AutoSize","","# Long-running work without blocking the console","Invoke-Command -ComputerName $servers -ScriptBlock { Get-HotFix } -AsJob","Get-Job | Receive-Job -Keep"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: -ComputerName accepts an array and fans the script block out in parallel, returning deserialised objects tagged with PSComputerName. -AsJob backgrounds the whole operation. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Variables from the local session are not available inside the script block. Referencing $threshold defined outside it silently evaluates to null unless you pass it with -ArgumentList or the $using: scope modifier. WHY IT MATTERS: Invoke-Command syntax is reported as being tested literally on AZ-802, including which parameters it takes."},{"id":18,"title":"Solve the PowerShell remoting double-hop problem","level":"ADV","cat":"Remote Management","purpose":"Configure resource-based constrained delegation so a remote session can reach a second server.","config":["# The problem: from SRV01, reaching a share on SRV02 fails with Access Denied","Invoke-Command -ComputerName SRV01 -ScriptBlock { Get-ChildItem \\\\SRV02\\Data }","","# Fix, configured ON THE RESOURCE (SRV02 decides who may delegate to it)","$srv01 = Get-ADComputer SRV01","Set-ADComputer SRV02 -PrincipalsAllowedToDelegateToAccount $srv01","","# Verify","Get-ADComputer SRV02 -Properties PrincipalsAllowedToDelegateToAccount |"," Select-Object -ExpandProperty PrincipalsAllowedToDelegateToAccount","","# Clear the Kerberos ticket cache on SRV01 so the change takes effect","Invoke-Command -ComputerName SRV01 -ScriptBlock { klist purge -li 0x3e7 }"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: Resource-based constrained delegation is configured on the target resource, so the resource owner controls who may delegate to it. It works across domains and needs no domain-wide privilege. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: CredSSP also solves the double hop but forwards the actual credential to the intermediate server, where it can be stolen. It is the distractor answer whenever delegation is available. WHY IT MATTERS: The double-hop problem and its correct fix are explicitly listed in the AZ-802 remote management objectives."},{"id":19,"title":"Build a Just Enough Administration endpoint","level":"ADV","cat":"Remote Management","purpose":"Restrict a service desk group to a named set of cmdlets running under a temporary virtual account.","config":["# 1. Role capability - exactly what may be run","$rcPath = 'C:\\Program Files\\WindowsPowerShell\\Modules\\HelpDesk\\RoleCapabilities'","New-Item -Path $rcPath -ItemType Directory -Force","New-PSRoleCapabilityFile -Path \"$rcPath\\HelpDesk.psrc\" `"," -VisibleCmdlets 'Get-Service','Get-EventLog',"," @{ Name='Restart-Service'; Parameters=@{ Name='Name'; ValidateSet='Spooler','W32Time' } }","","# 2. Session configuration - who gets which role","New-PSSessionConfigurationFile -Path 'C:\\JEA\\HelpDesk.pssc' `"," -SessionType RestrictedRemoteServer -RunAsVirtualAccount `"," -TranscriptDirectory 'C:\\JEA\\Transcripts' `"," -RoleDefinitions @{ 'CORP\\GG-HelpDesk' = @{ RoleCapabilities = 'HelpDesk' } }","","Register-PSSessionConfiguration -Name 'HelpDesk' -Path 'C:\\JEA\\HelpDesk.pssc' -Force","","# 3. Connect and confirm the restriction","Enter-PSSession -ComputerName SRV01 -ConfigurationName 'HelpDesk'","Get-Command"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: RestrictedRemoteServer strips the session down to a handful of built-ins, and the role capability adds back only the named cmdlets. RunAsVirtualAccount executes them under a temporary local administrator that exists only for the session. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Omitting -RunAsVirtualAccount leaves the session running as the connecting user, who still needs administrative rights — which defeats the entire purpose of JEA. WHY IT MATTERS: JEA is named explicitly in the AZ-802 remote management objectives as a way to limit the scope of administrative access."},{"id":20,"title":"Enable OpenSSH server and use PowerShell over SSH","level":"INTER","cat":"Remote Management","purpose":"Install the OpenSSH server feature and establish a cross-platform remoting session.","config":["Add-WindowsCapability -Online -Name OpenSSH.Server~~~~0.0.1.0","Start-Service sshd","Set-Service -Name sshd -StartupType Automatic","","# Confirm the firewall rule exists and is enabled","Get-NetFirewallRule -Name *OpenSSH-Server* | Select-Object Name,Enabled,Direction","","# Register PowerShell as an SSH subsystem in sshd_config:","# Subsystem powershell c:/progra~1/powershell/7/pwsh.exe -sshs -NoLogo","Restart-Service sshd","","# Connect using SSH transport rather than WinRM","Enter-PSSession -HostName srv01.corp.contoso.com -UserName admin","New-PSSession -HostName srv01.corp.contoso.com -UserName admin -KeyFilePath ~\\.ssh\\id_ed25519"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: PowerShell 7 registers itself as an SSH subsystem, so -HostName uses SSH rather than WinRM. That works to and from Linux without Kerberos or domain membership. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Using -ComputerName instead of -HostName forces the WinRM transport, which needs TrustedHosts or domain authentication and will fail against a non-domain or Linux target. WHY IT MATTERS: Remote SSH is explicitly listed in the AZ-802 hybrid management objectives alongside WinRM and RDP."},{"id":21,"title":"Onboard an on-premises server to Azure Arc","level":"CORE","cat":"Azure Arc","purpose":"Install the Connected Machine agent and register the server as an Azure resource.","config":["# Download and install the agent","Invoke-WebRequest -Uri 'https://aka.ms/AzureConnectedMachineAgent' `"," -OutFile AzureConnectedMachineAgent.msi","msiexec /i AzureConnectedMachineAgent.msi /qn","","$azcm = \"$env:ProgramFiles\\AzureConnectedMachineAgent\\azcmagent.exe\"","","& $azcm connect `"," --resource-group 'rg-arc-servers' `"," --tenant-id '8f4c2a10-6b3e-4d92-a5c7-1e0f8b3d4a26' `"," --subscription-id 'd91b7c33-2e14-4a88-9f60-77b1c8e5a204' `"," --location 'uksouth' `"," --tags 'Environment=Production,Owner=PlatformTeam'","","& $azcm show"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: The Connected Machine agent projects the server into Azure Resource Manager as a Microsoft.HybridCompute/machines resource, after which policy, monitoring, patching, and extensions all apply to it. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Onboarding without tags means the machine cannot be selected by dynamic scoping in Azure Update Manager or targeted by tag-based policy, so it silently misses patch cycles. WHY IT MATTERS: Azure Arc is the expanded area in the AZ-802 blueprint and azcmagent syntax is reported as being tested specifically."},{"id":22,"title":"Diagnose a disconnected Azure Arc agent","level":"INTER","cat":"Azure Arc","purpose":"Check agent status and test connectivity to every endpoint Arc requires.","config":["$azcm = \"$env:ProgramFiles\\AzureConnectedMachineAgent\\azcmagent.exe\"","","& $azcm show","# Agent Status : Disconnected","# Last Heartbeat : 2026-07-25 14:22:08","","# Test every required endpoint","& $azcm check","","# Confirm the local services are running","Get-Service himds,GCArcService,ExtensionService |"," Select-Object Name,Status,StartType","","# Proxy configuration, if the environment requires one","& $azcm config set proxy.url 'http://proxy.corp.contoso.com:3128'","Restart-Service himds"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: azcmagent check performs a connectivity test against each Azure endpoint the agent needs and reports which are reachable, which turns a vague 'Disconnected' into a specific blocked hostname. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Restarting the himds service does not help when a firewall is blocking an endpoint — the agent reconnects, fails the same way, and returns to Disconnected. Fix the network path first. WHY IT MATTERS: Arc extension and agent troubleshooting is named explicitly in the AZ-802 troubleshooting objectives."},{"id":23,"title":"Schedule patching with Azure Update Manager and dynamic scoping","level":"INTER","cat":"Azure Update Manager","purpose":"Create a maintenance configuration that targets machines by tag rather than by a static list.","config":["Connect-AzAccount","","New-AzMaintenanceConfiguration -ResourceGroupName 'rg-updates' `"," -Name 'mc-monthly-servers' -Location 'uksouth' `"," -MaintenanceScope 'InGuestPatch' `"," -StartDateTime '2026-08-02 02:00' -Duration '03:00' `"," -RecurEvery '1Month Second Sunday' -Timezone 'GMT Standard Time' `"," -WindowsParameterClassificationToInclude 'Critical','Security' `"," -InstallPatchRebootSetting 'IfRequired'","","# Dynamic scope - machines are selected by tag, not by name","New-AzConfigurationAssignment -ResourceGroupName 'rg-updates' `"," -MaintenanceConfigurationId $mc.Id `"," -ConfigurationAssignmentName 'prod-servers' `"," -Filter @{ tagSettings = @{ tags = @{ Environment = @('Production') } } }"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: A maintenance configuration defines when patching runs; a dynamic scope defines which machines it covers, evaluated at run time so newly tagged servers are included automatically. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: A static assignment list goes stale the moment a server is built or decommissioned, so new machines silently never get patched. Update Manager also does not host update content — machines still fetch from Windows Update or WSUS. WHY IT MATTERS: Azure Update Manager replaced Automation Update Management in this blueprint and is one of the flagged new topics."},{"id":24,"title":"Run an Azure Automation runbook against tagged servers","level":"ADV","cat":"Automation","purpose":"Use a managed identity and Invoke-AzVMRunCommand to act on a fleet.","config":["# Runbook body - authenticates with the Automation account's managed identity","Connect-AzAccount -Identity","","$vms = Get-AzVM | Where-Object { $_.Tags['Role'] -eq 'Web' }","","foreach ($vm in $vms) {"," Write-Output \"Processing $($vm.Name)\""," Invoke-AzVMRunCommand -ResourceGroupName $vm.ResourceGroupName `"," -VMName $vm.Name -CommandId 'RunPowerShellScript' `"," -ScriptString 'Restart-Service -Name W3SVC -Force; Get-Service W3SVC'","}","","# For on-premises or Arc machines, run on an extension-based","# Hybrid Runbook Worker instead of the Azure sandbox"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: Connect-AzAccount -Identity uses the Automation account's managed identity, so no credential is stored anywhere. Invoke-AzVMRunCommand executes inside the guest without needing network access to it. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Running against Arc-enabled or on-premises servers from the Azure sandbox fails, because the sandbox has no route to them. Those need an extension-based Hybrid Runbook Worker. WHY IT MATTERS: Automation runbooks and extension-based hybrid workers are both listed in the AZ-802 hybrid management objectives."},{"id":25,"title":"Create a Hyper-V virtual switch and configure VLAN trunking","level":"CORE","cat":"Hyper-V","purpose":"Build an external switch and set a VM adapter to access or trunk mode.","config":["New-VMSwitch -Name 'vSwitch-Ext' -NetAdapterName 'Ethernet 2' `"," -AllowManagementOS $true","","Connect-VMNetworkAdapter -VMName 'APP01' -SwitchName 'vSwitch-Ext'","","# Access mode - a single VLAN","Set-VMNetworkAdapterVlan -VMName 'APP01' -Access -VlanId 100","","# Trunk mode - multiple VLANs plus a native VLAN","Set-VMNetworkAdapterVlan -VMName 'FW01' -Trunk `"," -AllowedVlanIdList '10,20,30' -NativeVlanId 1","","Get-VMNetworkAdapterVlan -VMName 'FW01' |"," Select-Object VMName,OperationMode,AccessVlanId,AllowedVlanIdListString,NativeVlanId"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: -Access with -VlanId tags all traffic from that adapter with one VLAN. -Trunk requires both -AllowedVlanIdList and -NativeVlanId, which is what a virtual firewall or router VM needs. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Supplying -Trunk without -NativeVlanId is rejected. Supplying -VlanId with -Trunk is also wrong — the allowed list is the trunk equivalent. WHY IT MATTERS: Set-VMNetworkAdapterVlan is reported as appearing on the live AZ-802 exam as an incomplete-syntax question."},{"id":26,"title":"Configure Dynamic Memory on a virtual machine","level":"CORE","cat":"Hyper-V","purpose":"Set startup, minimum, maximum, buffer, and weight for a workload that benefits from density.","config":["Set-VMMemory -VMName 'APP01' -DynamicMemoryEnabled $true `"," -MinimumBytes 1GB -StartupBytes 4GB -MaximumBytes 16GB `"," -Buffer 20 -Priority 80","","Get-VMMemory -VMName 'APP01' |"," Select-Object VMName,DynamicMemoryEnabled,Minimum,Startup,Maximum,Buffer,Priority","","# Static memory for workloads that manage their own - SQL, Exchange","Set-VMMemory -VMName 'SQL01' -DynamicMemoryEnabled $false -StartupBytes 32GB","","# Current demand versus assigned","Get-VM | Select-Object Name,MemoryAssigned,MemoryDemand,MemoryStatus"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: Dynamic Memory lets the host reclaim unused memory from idle guests and give it to busy ones. Buffer keeps headroom above current demand; Priority decides who wins when the host is short. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Enabling Dynamic Memory on SQL Server or Exchange causes those applications to misjudge available memory and behave badly, because they allocate based on what they see at startup. WHY IT MATTERS: Configuring VM memory settings is named directly in the AZ-802 virtual machine objectives."},{"id":27,"title":"Enable nested virtualization for a lab guest","level":"INTER","cat":"Hyper-V","purpose":"Expose virtualization extensions to a VM so it can run Hyper-V itself.","config":["# The VM must be powered off","Stop-VM -Name 'HV-LAB'","","Set-VMProcessor -VMName 'HV-LAB' -ExposeVirtualizationExtensions $true","","# Dynamic Memory is not supported with nested virtualization","Set-VMMemory -VMName 'HV-LAB' -DynamicMemoryEnabled $false -StartupBytes 16GB","","# Required so nested guests can reach the network","Set-VMNetworkAdapter -VMName 'HV-LAB' -MacAddressSpoofing On","","Start-VM -Name 'HV-LAB'","Get-VMProcessor -VMName 'HV-LAB' | Select-Object VMName,ExposeVirtualizationExtensions"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: ExposeVirtualizationExtensions passes the CPU virtualization features through to the guest so it can run a hypervisor of its own. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Leaving Dynamic Memory enabled prevents nested virtualization from working at all, and forgetting MAC address spoofing leaves the nested guests with no network connectivity even though the host VM works. WHY IT MATTERS: Nested virtualization is listed explicitly in the AZ-802 Hyper-V objectives."},{"id":28,"title":"Assign GPU resources: DDA versus GPU partitioning","level":"ADV","cat":"Hyper-V","purpose":"Give one VM an entire GPU, or share a single GPU across several guests.","config":["# GPU partitioning - share one GPU across several VMs","Get-VMHostPartitionableGpu | Select-Object Name,ValidPartitionCounts","","Add-VMGpuPartitionAdapter -VMName 'VDI01'","Set-VMGpuPartitionAdapter -VMName 'VDI01' `"," -MinPartitionVRAM 1GB -MaxPartitionVRAM 4GB -OptimalPartitionVRAM 2GB","","# Discrete Device Assignment - the whole GPU to one VM","$dev = Get-PnpDevice | Where-Object { $_.Class -eq 'Display' -and $_.Status -eq 'OK' }","$locationPath = (Get-PnpDeviceProperty -InstanceId $dev.InstanceId `"," -KeyName DEVPKEY_Device_LocationPaths).Data[0]","","Disable-PnpDevice -InstanceId $dev.InstanceId -Confirm:$false","Dismount-VMHostAssignableDevice -LocationPath $locationPath -Force","Add-VMAssignableDevice -VMName 'ML01' -LocationPath $locationPath"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: GPU partitioning divides one physical GPU among several guests, each getting a VRAM slice. DDA dismounts the device from the host entirely and passes it through to a single VM at native performance. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Attempting DDA without first disabling and dismounting the device from the host fails, because the host driver still owns it. Neither mechanism supports live migration. WHY IT MATTERS: GPU partitioning is new to the AZ-802 blueprint, and choosing between it and DDA is a stated exam scenario."},{"id":29,"title":"Create and manage production checkpoints","level":"INTER","cat":"Hyper-V","purpose":"Take an application-consistent checkpoint before a change and roll back if needed.","config":["# Production checkpoints use VSS inside the guest","Set-VM -VMName 'APP01' -CheckpointType Production","","Checkpoint-VM -Name 'APP01' -SnapshotName 'Pre-patch 2026-07-27'","","Get-VMSnapshot -VMName 'APP01' |"," Select-Object Name,SnapshotType,CreationTime,ParentSnapshotName","","# Roll back","Restore-VMSnapshot -Name 'Pre-patch 2026-07-27' -VMName 'APP01' -Confirm:$false","","# Always remove checkpoints once the change is confirmed","Get-VMSnapshot -VMName 'APP01' | Remove-VMSnapshot"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: Production checkpoints quiesce the guest with VSS so the captured state is application-consistent and safe to restore, unlike a standard checkpoint which saves raw memory state. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Restoring a domain controller from a standard checkpoint can cause USN rollback and directory corruption. Checkpoints also grow a differencing chain that degrades performance the longer they are kept. WHY IT MATTERS: Managing VM checkpoints is a stated AZ-802 objective, and the production versus standard distinction is the tested part."},{"id":30,"title":"Create an AD-integrated DNS zone with secure dynamic updates","level":"CORE","cat":"DNS","purpose":"Build a forest-scoped zone and add the records a file server needs.","config":["Add-DnsServerPrimaryZone -Name 'corp.contoso.com' `"," -ReplicationScope 'Forest' -DynamicUpdate 'Secure'","","Add-DnsServerResourceRecordA -ZoneName 'corp.contoso.com' `"," -Name 'fileserver' -IPv4Address '10.1.10.50' -CreatePtr","","Add-DnsServerResourceRecordCName -ZoneName 'corp.contoso.com' `"," -Name 'files' -HostNameAlias 'fileserver.corp.contoso.com'","","Get-DnsServerZone |"," Select-Object ZoneName,ZoneType,IsDsIntegrated,ReplicationScope,DynamicUpdate"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: An AD-integrated zone is multi-master, so any DC running DNS can accept updates, and it replicates through AD rather than by zone transfer. Secure dynamic update restricts record changes to the object that owns the record. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Setting -DynamicUpdate to NonsecureAndSecure lets any host overwrite any record, which is a straightforward spoofing path. -CreatePtr silently does nothing if no reverse lookup zone exists. WHY IT MATTERS: AD-integrated DNS and its replication scopes are core to the AZ-802 networking domain."},{"id":31,"title":"Configure a conditional forwarder replicated across the forest","level":"INTER","cat":"DNS","purpose":"Resolve a partner or Azure private namespace without creating a trust.","config":["# General forwarder for internet resolution","Set-DnsServerForwarder -IPAddress '8.8.8.8','1.1.1.1' -UseRootHint $false","","# Conditional forwarder for one specific namespace","Add-DnsServerConditionalForwarderZone -Name 'partner.local' `"," -MasterServers '192.0.2.53' -ReplicationScope 'Forest'","","# Azure private endpoint namespace, via a forwarder VM in the VNet","Add-DnsServerConditionalForwarderZone `"," -Name 'privatelink.blob.core.windows.net' `"," -MasterServers '10.20.0.4' -ReplicationScope 'Forest'","","Get-DnsServerZone | Where-Object ZoneType -eq 'Forwarder' |"," Select-Object ZoneName,MasterServers"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: -ReplicationScope Forest stores the conditional forwarder in Active Directory so every DNS server in the forest receives it automatically and resolution is consistent. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Pointing a conditional forwarder directly at 168.63.129.16 fails, because the Azure DNS wire IP is only reachable from inside a virtual network. It must point at a forwarder VM or an Azure DNS Private Resolver inbound endpoint. WHY IT MATTERS: Hybrid name resolution and the 168.63.129.16 conditional-forwarder scenario are both reported as appearing on AZ-802."},{"id":32,"title":"Sign a DNS zone with DNSSEC","level":"ADV","cat":"DNS","purpose":"Enable origin authentication for a zone and confirm the signing state.","config":["Invoke-DnsServerZoneSign -ZoneName 'corp.contoso.com' -SignWithDefault -Force","","Get-DnsServerDnsSecZoneSetting -ZoneName 'corp.contoso.com' |"," Select-Object ZoneName,IsSigned,DenialOfExistence,NSec3HashAlgorithm","","# Inspect the generated signing keys","Get-DnsServerSigningKey -ZoneName 'corp.contoso.com' |"," Select-Object KeyId,KeyType,CryptoAlgorithm,IsRolloverEnabled","","# Clients enforce validation via the Name Resolution Policy Table (GPO):","# Computer Configuration > Policies > Windows Settings > Name Resolution Policy"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: Zone signing generates RRSIG signatures over each record set plus DNSKEY records for verification, so a resolver can prove the answer came from the authoritative server unaltered. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Signing the zone alone changes nothing for clients — they must be told to require validation through the NRPT, or they will happily accept unsigned answers. WHY IT MATTERS: DNSSEC is listed in the AZ-802 name resolution objectives, and the authenticate-not-encrypt distinction is tested."},{"id":33,"title":"Enable DNS scavenging to remove stale records","level":"INTER","cat":"DNS","purpose":"Configure no-refresh and refresh intervals at both server and zone level.","config":["# Server level","Set-DnsServerScavenging -ScavengingState $true `"," -ScavengingInterval 7.00:00:00 `"," -RefreshInterval 7.00:00:00 -NoRefreshInterval 7.00:00:00 `"," -ApplyOnAllZones","","Get-DnsServerScavenging","","# Zone level must also be enabled","Set-DnsServerZoneAging -Name 'corp.contoso.com' -Aging $true `"," -RefreshInterval 7.00:00:00 -NoRefreshInterval 7.00:00:00","","Get-DnsServerZoneAging -Name 'corp.contoso.com'"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: Scavenging removes dynamically registered records that have not refreshed within the combined no-refresh plus refresh window, which prevents stale entries pointing at reassigned addresses. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Enabling scavenging at the server without enabling aging on the zone does nothing. Enabling it on a long-neglected zone can delete a large number of records in one pass — review before turning it on. WHY IT MATTERS: Stale DNS records are a stated cause of the intermittent name resolution failures AZ-802 asks you to troubleshoot."},{"id":34,"title":"Install, authorise, and scope a DHCP server","level":"CORE","cat":"DHCP","purpose":"Deploy the role, authorise it in AD, and create a scope with options and a reservation.","config":["Install-WindowsFeature DHCP -IncludeManagementTools","","# Authorisation in AD is mandatory or the server leases nothing","Add-DhcpServerInDC -DnsName 'dhcp01.corp.contoso.com' -IPAddress '10.1.1.10'","Get-DhcpServerInDC","","Add-DhcpServerv4Scope -Name 'VLAN10-Staff' `"," -StartRange '10.1.10.50' -EndRange '10.1.10.250' `"," -SubnetMask '255.255.255.0' -LeaseDuration 8.00:00:00","","Add-DhcpServerv4ExclusionRange -ScopeId '10.1.10.0' `"," -StartRange '10.1.10.50' -EndRange '10.1.10.59'","","Set-DhcpServerv4OptionValue -ScopeId '10.1.10.0' `"," -Router '10.1.10.1' -DnsServer '10.1.1.10','10.1.1.11' `"," -DnsDomain 'corp.contoso.com'","","Add-DhcpServerv4Reservation -ScopeId '10.1.10.0' `"," -IPAddress '10.1.10.55' -ClientId '00-1A-2B-3C-4D-5E' `"," -Description 'Reception printer'"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: Add-DhcpServerInDC authorises the server in Active Directory, which is what permits it to respond to DHCP requests at all in a domain environment. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: A correctly configured but unauthorised DHCP server hands out nothing and logs an authorisation failure — the symptom looks like a network problem rather than a configuration one. WHY IT MATTERS: DHCP scopes, reservations, and authorisation are all named in the AZ-802 IP addressing objectives."},{"id":35,"title":"Configure DHCP failover between two servers","level":"INTER","cat":"DHCP","purpose":"Set up load-balanced failover so a scope survives the loss of one server.","config":["Add-DhcpServerv4Failover -Name 'DHCP01-DHCP02' `"," -PartnerServer 'dhcp02.corp.contoso.com' `"," -ScopeId '10.1.10.0' `"," -LoadBalancePercent 50 `"," -SharedSecret 'S3cret!' `"," -MaxClientLeadTime 1:00:00 `"," -AutoStateTransition $true","","Get-DhcpServerv4Failover |"," Select-Object Name,Mode,State,PartnerServer,LoadBalancePercent,MaxClientLeadTime","","# Hot standby instead, for a branch server backed by the datacentre","Add-DhcpServerv4Failover -Name 'Branch-HotStandby' `"," -PartnerServer 'dhcp-hq.corp.contoso.com' -ScopeId '10.5.0.0' `"," -ServerRole Active -ReservePercent 5 -SharedSecret 'S3cret!'"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: Load balance mode has both servers leasing simultaneously from a split pool. Hot standby designates one active and one reserve. MaxClientLeadTime bounds how long a partner may extend leases on its own authority. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: MaxClientLeadTime must match on both partners. A mismatch prevents the relationship reaching Normal state, and the scope remains unprotected despite appearing configured. WHY IT MATTERS: DHCP failover appeared in the case study on the live AZ-802 exam and is a stated high-availability objective."},{"id":36,"title":"Initialise a disk and create a formatted volume","level":"CORE","cat":"Storage","purpose":"Bring a new raw disk online with GPT partitioning and an NTFS volume.","config":["Get-Disk | Where-Object PartitionStyle -eq 'RAW' |"," Select-Object Number,FriendlyName,Size,PartitionStyle","","Initialize-Disk -Number 2 -PartitionStyle GPT","","New-Partition -DiskNumber 2 -UseMaximumSize -DriveLetter E","","Format-Volume -DriveLetter E -FileSystem NTFS `"," -AllocationUnitSize 65536 -NewFileSystemLabel 'Data' -Confirm:$false","","Get-Volume -DriveLetter E |"," Select-Object DriveLetter,FileSystemLabel,FileSystem,Size,SizeRemaining"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: GPT is required for UEFI boot and supports volumes beyond 2 TB. A 64 KB allocation unit suits large sequential files such as database and backup volumes. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Choosing MBR caps the disk at 2 TB and limits you to four primary partitions. A 64 KB cluster on a volume full of small files wastes substantial space in slack. WHY IT MATTERS: Configuring disks and volumes is a stated AZ-802 storage objective."},{"id":37,"title":"Build a Storage Spaces pool with a mirrored virtual disk","level":"INTER","cat":"Storage","purpose":"Pool physical disks and create a resilient virtual disk on top.","config":["$disks = Get-PhysicalDisk -CanPool $true","$disks | Select-Object FriendlyName,MediaType,Size","","New-StoragePool -FriendlyName 'Pool01' `"," -StorageSubSystemFriendlyName (Get-StorageSubSystem).FriendlyName `"," -PhysicalDisks $disks","","New-VirtualDisk -StoragePoolFriendlyName 'Pool01' -FriendlyName 'Data' `"," -ResiliencySettingName 'Mirror' -NumberOfDataCopies 2 `"," -ProvisioningType Fixed -UseMaximumSize","","Get-VirtualDisk |"," Select-Object FriendlyName,ResiliencySettingName,ProvisioningType,Size,HealthStatus"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: A two-way mirror keeps two copies and tolerates a single disk failure. Fixed provisioning allocates capacity up front so the pool cannot be over-committed. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Thin provisioning lets you over-commit the pool, which is efficient until it actually fills — at which point every thin virtual disk stops accepting writes simultaneously. WHY IT MATTERS: Storage Spaces configuration and resiliency choices are named directly in the AZ-802 storage objectives."},{"id":38,"title":"Enable Storage Spaces Direct on a cluster","level":"ADV","cat":"Storage","purpose":"Validate, cluster, and enable S2D, then create a CSV volume.","config":["# Validate before clustering","Test-Cluster -Node 'S2D01','S2D02','S2D03','S2D04' `"," -Include 'Storage Spaces Direct','Inventory','Network','System Configuration'","","New-Cluster -Name 'S2DCluster' -Node 'S2D01','S2D02','S2D03','S2D04' `"," -StaticAddress '10.1.50.20' -NoStorage","","Enable-ClusterStorageSpacesDirect -Confirm:$false","","New-Volume -StoragePoolFriendlyName 'S2D*' -FriendlyName 'VMs' `"," -FileSystem CSVFS_ReFS -ResiliencySettingName Mirror -Size 4TB","","Get-ClusterStorageSpacesDirect | Select-Object State,CacheState,CacheModeSSD"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: -NoStorage prevents the cluster claiming disks before S2D is enabled. Enable-ClusterStorageSpacesDirect pools the local disks of every node into one shared pool, and CSVFS_ReFS gives cluster-shared ReFS for VM storage. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: S2D requires Windows Server Datacenter edition. On Standard edition Enable-ClusterStorageSpacesDirect fails outright, regardless of how the hardware is configured. WHY IT MATTERS: Implementing and managing Storage Spaces Direct is a stated AZ-802 objective, and the Datacenter edition requirement is a tested licensing detail."},{"id":39,"title":"Configure Storage Replica between two servers","level":"ADV","cat":"Storage","purpose":"Test the topology, then establish synchronous block-level replication.","config":["Install-WindowsFeature Storage-Replica,FS-FileServer -IncludeManagementTools -Restart","","# Validate first - checks latency, throughput, and log sizing","Test-SRTopology -SourceComputerName 'SRV01' -SourceVolumeName 'E:' `"," -SourceLogVolumeName 'L:' -DestinationComputerName 'SRV02' `"," -DestinationVolumeName 'E:' -DestinationLogVolumeName 'L:' `"," -DurationInMinutes 30 -ResultPath 'C:\\Temp'","","New-SRPartnership -SourceComputerName 'SRV01' -SourceRGName 'RG01' `"," -SourceVolumeName 'E:' -SourceLogVolumeName 'L:' `"," -DestinationComputerName 'SRV02' -DestinationRGName 'RG02' `"," -DestinationVolumeName 'E:' -DestinationLogVolumeName 'L:' `"," -ReplicationMode Synchronous","","Get-SRGroup | Select-Object Name,ComputerName,ReplicationStatus"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: Synchronous replication acknowledges a write only once both sites have committed it, giving an RPO of zero. The separate log volume absorbs write bursts and should be on fast storage. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: The destination volume is dismounted and inaccessible for the duration of the partnership. Expecting to read from it, back it up, or use it actively is a common misunderstanding. WHY IT MATTERS: Storage Replica configuration is a stated AZ-802 objective, and the inaccessible-destination behaviour is the tested detail."},{"id":40,"title":"Enable data deduplication on a volume","level":"INTER","cat":"Storage","purpose":"Turn on dedup with an appropriate usage type and check the savings.","config":["Install-WindowsFeature FS-Data-Deduplication","","Enable-DedupVolume -Volume 'E:' -UsageType Default","","Set-DedupVolume -Volume 'E:' -MinimumFileAgeDays 3 `"," -ExcludeFileType 'vhd,vhdx' -OptimizeInUseFiles","","Start-DedupJob -Volume 'E:' -Type Optimization -Memory 50 -Priority Normal","","Get-DedupStatus -Volume 'E:' |"," Select-Object Volume,SavedSpace,SavingsRate,OptimizedFilesCount","","Get-DedupJob | Select-Object Type,Volume,Progress,State"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: The usage type tunes the chunking and scheduling for the workload: Default for general file servers, Hyper-V for VDI, Backup for virtualised backup targets. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Choosing the Default usage type for a Hyper-V VDI volume produces far worse savings and can affect VM performance, because it is not tuned for open VHDX files. WHY IT MATTERS: Configuring data deduplication is a stated AZ-802 storage objective."},{"id":41,"title":"Enable BitLocker and escrow the recovery key to Active Directory","level":"INTER","cat":"Storage","purpose":"Encrypt a volume and back up its recovery password to the computer object.","config":["Install-WindowsFeature BitLocker -IncludeAllSubFeature -Restart","","Enable-BitLocker -MountPoint 'C:' -EncryptionMethod XtsAes256 `"," -UsedSpaceOnly -TpmProtector","","Add-BitLockerKeyProtector -MountPoint 'C:' -RecoveryPasswordProtector","","$kp = (Get-BitLockerVolume -MountPoint 'C:').KeyProtector |"," Where-Object KeyProtectorType -eq 'RecoveryPassword'","Backup-BitLockerKeyProtector -MountPoint 'C:' -KeyProtectorId $kp.KeyProtectorId","","Get-BitLockerVolume |"," Select-Object MountPoint,VolumeStatus,ProtectionStatus,EncryptionPercentage"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: XtsAes256 is the modern cipher. Backup-BitLockerKeyProtector writes the 48-digit recovery password into the msFVE-RecoveryInformation object beneath the computer account. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: The GPO that escrows keys automatically must be in place before encryption begins. Volumes encrypted beforehand have no key in AD and must be backed up manually, exactly as shown here. WHY IT MATTERS: BitLocker recovery and configuring it with Group Policy are both reported as appearing on the live AZ-802 exam."},{"id":42,"title":"Recover a BitLocker-protected volume","level":"INTER","cat":"Storage","purpose":"Retrieve the recovery password from Active Directory and unlock a locked volume.","config":["# Find the recovery information stored under the computer object","$comp = Get-ADComputer 'SRV01'","Get-ADObject -Filter { objectClass -eq 'msFVE-RecoveryInformation' } `"," -SearchBase $comp.DistinguishedName `"," -Properties 'msFVE-RecoveryPassword','whenCreated' |"," Select-Object Name,whenCreated,msFVE-RecoveryPassword","","# Unlock a data volume with the recovery password","Unlock-BitLocker -MountPoint 'E:' -RecoveryPassword '123456-...-654321'","","# Suspend protection across a firmware update, then resume","Suspend-BitLocker -MountPoint 'C:' -RebootCount 2","Resume-BitLocker -MountPoint 'C:'"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: The recovery password is stored as a child object of the computer account, so retrieving it needs the computer's distinguished name as the search base and appropriate read rights. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Suspending BitLocker without -RebootCount leaves protection off indefinitely if the resume step is forgotten, which quietly removes the encryption guarantee. WHY IT MATTERS: Managing and recovering encrypted volumes is a stated AZ-802 storage objective."},{"id":43,"title":"Create an SMB share with access-based enumeration","level":"CORE","cat":"File Services","purpose":"Publish a share with layered permissions and hide what users cannot access.","config":["New-SmbShare -Name 'Finance' -Path 'E:\\Shares\\Finance' `"," -FullAccess 'CORP\\Domain Admins' `"," -ChangeAccess 'CORP\\DL-Finance-Modify' `"," -ReadAccess 'CORP\\DL-Finance-Read' `"," -FolderEnumerationMode AccessBased","","Get-SmbShare -Name 'Finance' |"," Select-Object Name,Path,FolderEnumerationMode,EncryptData","","Get-SmbShareAccess -Name 'Finance'","","# Encrypt this share's traffic in transit","Set-SmbShare -Name 'Finance' -EncryptData $true -Force"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: Effective access is the more restrictive of share and NTFS permissions. Access-based enumeration hides folders a user cannot read, which removes a great deal of confusion. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Access-based enumeration is not a security control — permissions still do the enforcing. Relying on it to protect data rather than to tidy the view is a misunderstanding. WHY IT MATTERS: Configuring access to Windows Server file shares and SMB settings are stated AZ-802 objectives."},{"id":44,"title":"Configure SMB over QUIC for VPN-less remote access","level":"ADV","cat":"File Services","purpose":"Map a server certificate so remote clients reach the share over UDP 443.","config":["# A server certificate whose SAN matches the public name","$cert = Get-ChildItem Cert:\\LocalMachine\\My |"," Where-Object Subject -eq 'CN=files.contoso.com'","","New-SmbServerCertificateMapping -Name 'files.contoso.com' `"," -Thumbprint $cert.Thumbprint -StoreName My","","Get-SmbServerCertificateMapping |"," Select-Object Name,Subject,Thumbprint,Type,Flags","","# Client connects normally - QUIC is negotiated automatically","net use Z: \\\\files.contoso.com\\Finance","","Get-SmbConnection | Select-Object ServerName,ShareName,Dialect,TransportName"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: SMB over QUIC carries SMB inside QUIC on UDP 443 with TLS 1.3 always on, so a remote user reaches an on-premises share securely without a VPN and without exposing port 445. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: A certificate whose subject alternative name does not match the name clients use is rejected during the QUIC handshake, and the client silently falls back to TCP 445 — which the firewall then blocks. WHY IT MATTERS: SMB over QUIC is one of the flagged new topics in the AZ-802 blueprint and is reported as appearing on the live exam."},{"id":45,"title":"Configure SMB Multichannel and Continuous Availability","level":"ADV","cat":"File Services","purpose":"Inspect multichannel connections and enable transparent failover on a clustered share.","config":["Get-SmbServerConfiguration |"," Select-Object EnableMultiChannel,EncryptData,RequireSecuritySignature,EnableSMB1Protocol","","# Which paths is a session actually using?","Get-SmbMultichannelConnection |"," Select-Object ServerName,ClientIpAddress,ServerIpAddress,ClientRSS,ClientRDMA","","Get-SmbMultichannelConstraint","","# Continuous Availability - transparent failover on a clustered share","Set-SmbShare -Name 'SQLData' -ContinuouslyAvailable $true -Force","","Get-SmbShare -Name 'SQLData' | Select-Object Name,ContinuouslyAvailable,Scoped"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: Multichannel uses several NICs or RSS queues for one SMB session, improving throughput and surviving the loss of a path. Continuous Availability makes a clustered share fail over without the application seeing an error. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Continuous Availability requires a failover cluster — it cannot be set on a standalone server. It also forces write-through, which slows general file shares, so it belongs on SQL and Hyper-V workloads only. WHY IT MATTERS: SMB Multichannel and Continuous Availability are both reported as appearing on the live AZ-802 exam."},{"id":46,"title":"Build a DFS namespace with two folder targets","level":"INTER","cat":"File Services","purpose":"Present shares from several servers under one logical path.","config":["Install-WindowsFeature FS-DFS-Namespace,FS-DFS-Replication -IncludeManagementTools","","New-DfsnRoot -TargetPath '\\\\FS01\\Shares' -Type DomainV2 `"," -Path '\\\\corp.contoso.com\\Shares'","","New-DfsnFolder -Path '\\\\corp.contoso.com\\Shares\\Finance' `"," -TargetPath '\\\\FS01\\Finance'","New-DfsnFolderTarget -Path '\\\\corp.contoso.com\\Shares\\Finance' `"," -TargetPath '\\\\FS02\\Finance'","","Get-DfsnFolderTarget -Path '\\\\corp.contoso.com\\Shares\\Finance' |"," Select-Object Path,TargetPath,State,ReferralPriorityClass"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: A domain-based namespace is stored in Active Directory and supports multiple namespace servers, so the path users have mapped keeps working when a file server is replaced. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: A standalone namespace lives on one server and becomes a single point of failure. Adding a second target without also configuring DFS Replication gives users two divergent copies of the data. WHY IT MATTERS: Implementing and configuring DFS is a stated AZ-802 file services objective."},{"id":47,"title":"Configure FSRM quotas and file screens","level":"INTER","cat":"File Services","purpose":"Apply a hard quota template and block executable files from a share.","config":["Install-WindowsFeature FS-Resource-Manager -IncludeManagementTools","","New-FsrmQuotaTemplate -Name '10GB Hard' -Size 10GB `"," -Threshold (New-FsrmQuotaThreshold -Percentage 85)","","New-FsrmQuota -Path 'E:\\Shares\\Users' -Template '10GB Hard'","","# Auto-apply to every new subfolder","New-FsrmAutoQuota -Path 'E:\\Shares\\Users' -Template '10GB Hard'","","New-FsrmFileGroup -Name 'Executables' -IncludePattern @('*.exe','*.bat','*.cmd','*.ps1')","New-FsrmFileScreen -Path 'E:\\Shares\\Finance' -IncludeGroup 'Executables' -Active","","Get-FsrmQuota | Select-Object Path,Size,Usage,SoftLimit"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: A hard quota blocks writes once the limit is reached; an auto-quota applies the template automatically to each new subfolder, which is what makes per-user home directories manageable. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Creating the file screen without -Active makes it passive: it reports and notifies but does not actually block the files, which looks configured but enforces nothing. WHY IT MATTERS: File Server Resource Manager is a stated AZ-802 file services objective."},{"id":48,"title":"Deploy Azure File Sync with cloud tiering","level":"ADV","cat":"File Services","purpose":"Register a server, create a sync group, and tier cold files to Azure.","config":["# On the server, after installing the Azure File Sync agent","Connect-AzAccount","Register-AzStorageSyncServer -ResourceGroupName 'rg-files' `"," -StorageSyncServiceName 'sss-contoso'","","New-AzStorageSyncGroup -ResourceGroupName 'rg-files' `"," -StorageSyncServiceName 'sss-contoso' -Name 'sg-finance'","","New-AzStorageSyncCloudEndpoint -ResourceGroupName 'rg-files' `"," -StorageSyncServiceName 'sss-contoso' -SyncGroupName 'sg-finance' `"," -StorageAccountResourceId $sa.Id -AzureFileShareName 'finance'","","New-AzStorageSyncServerEndpoint -ResourceGroupName 'rg-files' `"," -StorageSyncServiceName 'sss-contoso' -SyncGroupName 'sg-finance' `"," -ServerResourceId $serverId -ServerLocalPath 'E:\\Shares\\Finance' `"," -CloudTiering -VolumeFreeSpacePercent 20 -TierFilesOlderThanDays 30"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: The server endpoint caches hot data locally while the authoritative copy lives in the Azure file share. Cloud tiering can use a free-space policy, a date policy, or both together. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: A backup product that reads file contents recalls every tiered file, defeating the tiering and generating substantial egress. Use tiering-aware backup, or snapshot the Azure file share instead. WHY IT MATTERS: Azure File Sync and its cloud tiering Date policy are both reported as appearing on the live AZ-802 exam."},{"id":49,"title":"Deploy Windows LAPS with Active Directory storage","level":"ADV","cat":"Security","purpose":"Extend the schema, grant permissions, and retrieve a managed local administrator password.","config":["# One-time schema extension - requires Schema Admins","Update-LapsADSchema","","# Let computers write their own password","Set-LapsADComputerSelfPermission `"," -Identity 'OU=Servers,DC=corp,DC=contoso,DC=com'","","# Let an admin group read it","Set-LapsADReadPasswordPermission `"," -Identity 'OU=Servers,DC=corp,DC=contoso,DC=com' `"," -AllowedPrincipals 'CORP\\GG-ServerAdmins'","","# Retrieve a password","Get-LapsADPassword -Identity 'SRV01' -AsPlainText |"," Select-Object ComputerName,Account,Password,ExpirationTimestamp","","# Force an immediate rotation on the local machine","Reset-LapsPassword"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: The schema extension adds the LAPS attributes to computer objects. Each machine then generates and rotates its own unique local administrator password, and only the named principals can read it. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Update-LapsADSchema requires the Schema Master to be reachable and the caller to be in Schema Admins. Without it, every LAPS operation fails on a fresh domain — the most common deployment error. WHY IT MATTERS: Windows LAPS and the AD schema update are both reported as appearing on the live AZ-802 exam."},{"id":50,"title":"Apply a Windows Server security baseline with OSConfig","level":"ADV","cat":"Security","purpose":"Install the module, apply a baseline as desired state, and check compliance.","config":["Install-Module Microsoft.OSConfig -Scope AllUsers -Force","","# Apply the member server baseline as desired state","Set-OSConfigDesiredConfiguration `"," -Scenario 'SecurityBaseline/WS2025/MemberServer' -Default","","# Check compliance, including drift","Get-OSConfigDesiredConfiguration `"," -Scenario 'SecurityBaseline/WS2025/MemberServer' |"," Select-Object Name,Compliance,Reason","","# Domain controller baseline","Set-OSConfigDesiredConfiguration `"," -Scenario 'SecurityBaseline/WS2025/DomainController' -Default"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: OSConfig applies the baseline declaratively and can continuously remediate drift, rather than relying on a GPO staying applied and unedited. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Applying the member server baseline to a domain controller enforces the wrong setting set and can break directory operations. The scenario name has to match the machine's role. WHY IT MATTERS: OSConfig security baselines are one of the flagged new topics in the AZ-802 blueprint."},{"id":51,"title":"Create an Application Control policy in audit mode","level":"ADV","cat":"Security","purpose":"Generate a WDAC policy, run it in audit mode, and review what it would block.","config":["New-CIPolicy -Level Publisher -FilePath 'C:\\Temp\\Policy.xml' `"," -UserPEs -ScanPath 'C:\\Program Files' -Fallback Hash","","# Option 3 = Audit Mode: log, do not block","Set-RuleOption -FilePath 'C:\\Temp\\Policy.xml' -Option 3","","ConvertFrom-CIPolicy -XmlFilePath 'C:\\Temp\\Policy.xml' `"," -BinaryFilePath 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\CodeIntegrity\\SiPolicy.p7b'","","# Review what would have been blocked","Get-WinEvent -LogName 'Microsoft-Windows-CodeIntegrity/Operational' |"," Where-Object Id -in 3076,3077 |"," Select-Object TimeCreated,Id,Message -First 20","","# Only after review: remove option 3 to enforce","Set-RuleOption -FilePath 'C:\\Temp\\Policy.xml' -Option 3 -Delete"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: Publisher-level rules trust signed code from a given publisher, which survives application updates. Audit mode logs every would-be block to the CodeIntegrity log without preventing execution. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Enforcing a WDAC policy without an audit period can render a server unusable, and because it enforces in kernel mode, recovery may require booting to safe mode to remove the policy file.
