WHY IT MATTERS: Configuring Application Control for Windows is a stated AZ-802 security objective."},{"id":52,"title":"Configure Windows Firewall rules and IPsec connection security","level":"INTER","cat":"Security","purpose":"Allow a specific inbound service and require authenticated traffic between servers.","config":["Get-NetFirewallProfile |"," Select-Object Name,Enabled,DefaultInboundAction,DefaultOutboundAction,LogAllowed","","# Firewall rule - decides whether traffic is allowed","New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName 'Allow SQL from App tier' `"," -Direction Inbound -Protocol TCP -LocalPort 1433 `"," -RemoteAddress '10.1.20.0/24' -Action Allow -Profile Domain","","# Connection security rule - decides whether it must be authenticated","New-NetIPsecRule -DisplayName 'Require auth to SQL' `"," -InboundSecurity Require -OutboundSecurity Request `"," -Protocol TCP -LocalPort 1433 `"," -Phase1AuthSet (Get-NetIPsecPhase1AuthSet -Default).Name","","Get-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName 'Allow SQL*' |"," Get-NetFirewallPortFilter | Select-Object Protocol,LocalPort"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: A firewall rule permits or blocks traffic. A connection security rule is separate and governs whether that traffic must be authenticated or encrypted with IPsec — which is how domain and server isolation are built. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Creating only a firewall rule and expecting authentication does nothing; the traffic is allowed but unauthenticated. The two rule types are configured independently and both are needed. WHY IT MATTERS: Managing Windows Firewall including connection security rules is a stated AZ-802 security objective."},{"id":53,"title":"Audit Active Directory for dangerous delegation","level":"ADV","cat":"Security","purpose":"Find accounts trusted for unconstrained delegation and objects protected by AdminSDHolder.","config":["# Unconstrained delegation - a critical finding","Get-ADComputer -Filter { TrustedForDelegation -eq $true } `"," -Properties TrustedForDelegation,OperatingSystem |"," Select-Object Name,OperatingSystem,DistinguishedName","","Get-ADUser -Filter { TrustedForDelegation -eq $true } |"," Select-Object Name,SamAccountName","","# Accounts protected by AdminSDHolder","Get-ADUser -Filter { adminCount -eq 1 } -Properties adminCount |"," Select-Object Name,SamAccountName","","# Members of Protected Users","Get-ADGroupMember -Identity 'Protected Users' |"," Select-Object Name,objectClass","","# Enable directory change auditing","auditpol /set /subcategory:\"Directory Service Changes\" /success:enable /failure:enable"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: A server trusted for unconstrained delegation caches the full Kerberos TGT of every user who connects to it, so compromising that one server can yield a Domain Admin ticket. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Replacing unconstrained delegation with constrained delegation still trusts the intermediate server. Resource-based constrained delegation is stronger because the resource owner controls who may delegate to it. WHY IT MATTERS: Managing AD delegation and hardening domain controllers are both stated AZ-802 security objectives."},{"id":54,"title":"Create a fine-grained password policy for administrators","level":"INTER","cat":"Security","purpose":"Apply stricter password requirements to a privileged group only.","config":["New-ADFineGrainedPasswordPolicy -Name 'PSO-Admins' -Precedence 10 `"," -MinPasswordLength 20 -PasswordHistoryCount 24 `"," -MaxPasswordAge '90.00:00:00' -MinPasswordAge '1.00:00:00' `"," -LockoutThreshold 5 -LockoutDuration '00:30:00' `"," -LockoutObservationWindow '00:30:00' `"," -ComplexityEnabled $true -ReversibleEncryptionEnabled $false","","Add-ADFineGrainedPasswordPolicySubject -Identity 'PSO-Admins' `"," -Subjects 'GG-DomainAdmins'","","# Which policy actually applies to a given user?","Get-ADUserResultantPasswordPolicy -Identity 'admin.pnair' |"," Select-Object Name,MinPasswordLength,LockoutThreshold,MaxPasswordAge"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: Fine-grained password policies apply to users and global security groups, letting administrators have stricter requirements than the Default Domain Policy allows. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Only one policy ever applies — they do not merge. The lowest precedence value wins, and a policy linked directly to a user beats any group-linked policy regardless of precedence. WHY IT MATTERS: Configuring password policies is a stated AZ-802 security objective, and the precedence rule is the tested detail."},{"id":55,"title":"Attach and configure a managed data disk on an Azure VM","level":"INTER","cat":"Azure VMs","purpose":"Create a Premium SSD, attach it with correct caching, and prepare it in the guest.","config":["Connect-AzAccount","$vm = Get-AzVM -ResourceGroupName 'rg-prod' -Name 'SRV01'","","$cfg = New-AzDiskConfig -SkuName 'Premium_LRS' -Location 'uksouth' `"," -CreateOption Empty -DiskSizeGB 512","$disk = New-AzDisk -ResourceGroupName 'rg-prod' -DiskName 'SRV01-data01' -Disk $cfg","","# Caching None for write-heavy and database volumes","Add-AzVMDataDisk -VM $vm -Name 'SRV01-data01' -CreateOption Attach `"," -ManagedDiskId $disk.Id -Lun 0 -Caching None","Update-AzVM -VM $vm -ResourceGroupName 'rg-prod'","","# Then, inside the guest","Get-Disk | Where-Object PartitionStyle -eq 'RAW' |"," Initialize-Disk -PartitionStyle GPT -PassThru |"," New-Partition -AssignDriveLetter -UseMaximumSize |"," Format-Volume -FileSystem NTFS -Confirm:$false"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: Managed data disks persist across deallocation. Setting host caching to None is correct for write-heavy volumes and mandatory for the disk holding an AD DS database. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Placing data on the temporary disk (usually D:) loses it whenever the VM is deallocated or moves host. ReadWrite caching on a database volume risks write loss on host failure. WHY IT MATTERS: Managing storage for Windows Server VMs in Azure is a stated AZ-802 objective, and the DC disk-caching rule is tested."},{"id":56,"title":"Deploy Azure Bastion for RDP without a public IP","level":"INTER","cat":"Azure VMs","purpose":"Create the required subnet and a Bastion host for browser-based access.","config":["# The subnet name must be exactly AzureBastionSubnet, /26 or larger","$vnet = Get-AzVirtualNetwork -Name 'vnet-prod' -ResourceGroupName 'rg-prod'","Add-AzVirtualNetworkSubnetConfig -Name 'AzureBastionSubnet' `"," -VirtualNetwork $vnet -AddressPrefix '10.20.250.0/26'","$vnet | Set-AzVirtualNetwork","","$pip = New-AzPublicIpAddress -ResourceGroupName 'rg-prod' -Name 'pip-bastion' `"," -Location 'uksouth' -AllocationMethod Static -Sku Standard","","New-AzBastion -ResourceGroupName 'rg-prod' -Name 'bastion-prod' `"," -PublicIpAddress $pip -VirtualNetwork $vnet -Sku Standard","","Get-AzBastion -ResourceGroupName 'rg-prod' | Select-Object Name,Sku,ProvisioningState"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: Bastion connects to VMs over their private IP addresses, so the target VMs need no public IP and no inbound RDP rule from the internet. Access is over HTTPS from the portal. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: The subnet name is literal. Any other name causes deployment to fail, and a subnet smaller than /26 is rejected. WHY IT MATTERS: Managing just-in-time VM access and Azure Bastion is a stated AZ-802 objective, and the exact subnet name is a favourite tested detail."},{"id":57,"title":"Diagnose an Azure VM that will not accept connections","level":"ADV","cat":"Azure VMs","purpose":"Use boot diagnostics and Run Command to recover a VM locked out by its own firewall.","config":["Get-AzVM -ResourceGroupName 'rg-prod' -Name 'SRV01' -Status |"," Select-Object -ExpandProperty Statuses |"," Select-Object Code,DisplayStatus","","# Boot diagnostics - screenshot and serial log","Get-AzVMBootDiagnosticsData -ResourceGroupName 'rg-prod' -Name 'SRV01' `"," -Windows -LocalPath 'C:\\Temp'","","# Run Command works without network access to the VM","Invoke-AzVMRunCommand -ResourceGroupName 'rg-prod' -VMName 'SRV01' `"," -CommandId 'RunPowerShellScript' `"," -ScriptString 'Enable-NetFirewallRule -DisplayGroup \"Remote Desktop\"; Get-NetFirewallProfile | Select Name,Enabled'","","# Or use Serial Console, which needs boot diagnostics enabled"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: Run Command executes inside the guest through the VM agent rather than over the network, so it works when RDP and WinRM are unreachable. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Serial Console requires boot diagnostics to be enabled first, because it uses the same storage. If diagnostics were never turned on, that route is unavailable during the incident. WHY IT MATTERS: VM and extension troubleshooting, boot diagnostics, and Serial Console are all named in the AZ-802 troubleshooting objectives."},{"id":58,"title":"Capture a performance baseline with a data collector set","level":"INTER","cat":"Monitoring","purpose":"Record the key counters over time so future problems have something to compare against.","config":["$counters = @("," '\\Processor(_Total)\\% Processor Time',"," '\\System\\Processor Queue Length',"," '\\Memory\\Available MBytes',"," '\\Memory\\Pages/sec',"," '\\PhysicalDisk(_Total)\\Avg. Disk sec/Read',"," '\\PhysicalDisk(_Total)\\Current Disk Queue Length',"," '\\Network Interface(*)\\Bytes Total/sec'",")","","# Ad-hoc capture to a binary log","Get-Counter -Counter $counters -SampleInterval 5 -MaxSamples 720 |"," Export-Counter -Path 'C:\\PerfLogs\\baseline.blg' -Force","","# Persistent collector with circular logging","logman create counter 'Baseline' -c $counters -si 00:00:15 `"," -o 'C:\\PerfLogs\\Baseline' -f bincirc -max 500","logman start 'Baseline'","logman query 'Baseline'"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: A baseline captured while the server is healthy is what makes later data interpretable. Circular binary logging caps disk usage so the collector can run indefinitely. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Capturing only during an incident tells you what a broken server looks like with nothing to compare it against, which makes 'is 70% CPU normal here' unanswerable. WHY IT MATTERS: Monitoring with Performance Monitor and creating data collector sets are stated AZ-802 objectives."},{"id":59,"title":"Query Windows event logs efficiently","level":"CORE","cat":"Monitoring","purpose":"Filter at the log service rather than in PowerShell, and target the AD-specific logs.","config":["# Fast: the filter is evaluated by the event log service","Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{"," LogName = 'System'"," Level = 1,2"," StartTime = (Get-Date).AddHours(-24)","} | Select-Object TimeCreated,Id,ProviderName,Message -First 20","","# Directory Service log for AD problems","Get-WinEvent -LogName 'Directory Service' -MaxEvents 50 |"," Where-Object LevelDisplayName -in 'Error','Warning'","","# DFS Replication - 4602 means SYSVOL is shared","Get-WinEvent -LogName 'DFS Replication' -MaxEvents 20 |"," Where-Object Id -in 4602,4614,4604","","# Across many servers at once","Invoke-Command -ComputerName SRV01,SRV02 -ScriptBlock {"," Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{ LogName='System'; Level=1,2; StartTime=(Get-Date).AddDays(-1) }","}"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: -FilterHashtable pushes the query into the event log service so only matching events are returned, which on a busy server is the difference between seconds and minutes. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Piping Get-WinEvent -LogName System into Where-Object retrieves every event first and filters in PowerShell, which is dramatically slower and can time out on a heavily logged server. WHY IT MATTERS: Managing event logs is a stated AZ-802 monitoring objective, and these specific logs carry the AD diagnostics the exam asks about."},{"id":60,"title":"Deploy the Azure Monitor Agent with a data collection rule","level":"ADV","cat":"Monitoring","purpose":"Install the agent on an Azure or Arc machine and associate a DCR.","config":["# Azure VM","Set-AzVMExtension -ResourceGroupName 'rg-prod' -VMName 'SRV01' `"," -Name 'AzureMonitorWindowsAgent' `"," -Publisher 'Microsoft.Azure.Monitor' `"," -ExtensionType 'AzureMonitorWindowsAgent' `"," -TypeHandlerVersion '1.0' -Location 'uksouth' -EnableAutomaticUpgrade $true","","# Arc-enabled server - the same extension model","New-AzConnectedMachineExtension -ResourceGroupName 'rg-arc' `"," -MachineName 'SRV-FILE01' -Name 'AzureMonitorWindowsAgent' `"," -Publisher 'Microsoft.Azure.Monitor' `"," -ExtensionType 'AzureMonitorWindowsAgent' -Location 'uksouth'","","# Associate the data collection rule","New-AzDataCollectionRuleAssociation -TargetResourceId $vm.Id `"," -AssociationName 'dcr-windows-core' -RuleId $dcr.Id","","Get-AzDataCollectionRuleAssociation -TargetResourceId $vm.Id"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: The Azure Monitor Agent collects nothing until a data collection rule is associated with the machine. The same extension model works on Azure VMs and Arc-enabled servers alike. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: The retired Log Analytics agent was configured through workspace-level data sources. Documentation describing that model does not apply to AMA, where collection is defined entirely by DCRs. WHY IT MATTERS: Configuring data collection rules for Azure Monitor is a stated AZ-802 objective."},{"id":61,"title":"Find machines that have stopped reporting to Azure Monitor","level":"ADV","cat":"Monitoring","purpose":"Query the Heartbeat table so a silently failed agent does not go unnoticed.","config":["# KQL, run in Log Analytics or via Invoke-AzOperationalInsightsQuery","$query = @'","Heartbeat","| summarize LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated) by Computer, ResourceType","| where LastSeen < ago(30m)","| project Computer, ResourceType, LastSeen,"," MinutesAgo = datetime_diff(\"minute\", now(), LastSeen)","| order by MinutesAgo desc","'@","","Invoke-AzOperationalInsightsQuery -WorkspaceId $ws.CustomerId -Query $query |"," Select-Object -ExpandProperty Results","","# Promote it to a scheduled log alert so it runs continuously"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: A monitoring platform that silently loses a machine is worse than none, because you believe you have coverage. The Heartbeat table records every agent check-in, so absence is detectable. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Alerting only on metric thresholds misses this entirely — a dead agent reports no metrics at all, so no threshold is ever crossed and nothing fires. WHY IT MATTERS: Creating alerts and monitoring by using Azure services are stated AZ-802 objectives."},{"id":62,"title":"Diagnose and fix Windows Time service problems","level":"CORE","cat":"Troubleshooting","purpose":"Check the time hierarchy and correct a drifting domain controller or member server.","config":["w32tm /query /status","w32tm /query /configuration","","# Compare every DC in the domain","w32tm /monitor","","# Measure offset against a specific source","w32tm /stripchart /computer:DC01.corp.contoso.com /samples:5 /dataonly","","# PDC Emulator of the forest root - point at an external source","w32tm /config /manualpeerlist:'time.windows.com,0x8' `"," /syncfromflags:manual /reliable:yes /update","Restart-Service w32time","","# Any other member or DC - follow the domain hierarchy","w32tm /config /syncfromflags:domhier /update","Restart-Service w32time","w32tm /resync"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: Only the PDC Emulator of the forest root should use an external source; everything else follows the domain hierarchy. Kerberos rejects tickets beyond five minutes of skew, so time drift presents as authentication failure. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Configuring a member server or a non-PDC domain controller with an external manual peer creates two competing authorities and causes exactly the drift you were trying to fix. WHY IT MATTERS: Windows Time service troubleshooting is a new explicit addition to the AZ-802 objectives and underlies many apparent AD failures."},{"id":63,"title":"Repair a broken computer account secure channel","level":"INTER","cat":"Troubleshooting","purpose":"Test and reset the trust relationship without rejoining the domain.","config":["Test-ComputerSecureChannel -Verbose","# The secure channel between the local computer and the domain is broken.","","# Repair in place - no rejoin, no reboot required","Test-ComputerSecureChannel -Repair -Credential (Get-Credential)","","# Alternative, targeting a specific DC","Reset-ComputerMachinePassword -Server 'DC01.corp.contoso.com' `"," -Credential (Get-Credential)","","# Check for duplicate SPNs, a silent Kerberos failure","setspn -X","setspn -L 'CORP\\gMSA-SQL'","","klist","klist purge"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: Test-ComputerSecureChannel -Repair resets the computer account password on both sides, restoring the trust without the disruption of leaving and rejoining the domain. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Removing the machine from the domain and rejoining it creates a new computer object and loses group memberships, GPO links by security filtering, and any certificates bound to the old account. WHY IT MATTERS: Troubleshooting secure channel and computer account trust issues is a stated AZ-802 objective."},{"id":64,"title":"Detect and remove lingering objects","level":"ADV","cat":"Troubleshooting","purpose":"Identify objects on a DC that was offline beyond the tombstone lifetime and clean them up.","config":["# Check the tombstone lifetime","$cfg = (Get-ADRootDSE).configurationNamingContext","Get-ADObject -Identity \"CN=Directory Service,CN=Windows NT,CN=Services,$cfg\" `"," -Properties tombstoneLifetime | Select-Object tombstoneLifetime","","# Advisory mode first - reports without deleting","$srcGuid = (Get-ADDomainController -Identity DC01).InvocationId","repadmin /removelingeringobjects DC03 $srcGuid `"," 'DC=corp,DC=contoso,DC=com' /advisory_mode","","# Review event 1946 entries in the Directory Service log","Get-WinEvent -LogName 'Directory Service' |"," Where-Object Id -eq 1946 | Select-Object TimeCreated,Message","","# Then remove for real, omitting /advisory_mode"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: Advisory mode logs every lingering object it would remove without deleting anything, so you can confirm the scope before making an irreversible change against a reference DC you trust. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Running the removal without advisory mode first, or against the wrong reference DC, deletes objects that were legitimately created while the DC was offline. WHY IT MATTERS: Replication error 8606 and lingering objects fall under the AZ-802 AD troubleshooting objectives."},{"id":65,"title":"Reset Windows Update components on a stuck server","level":"INTER","cat":"Troubleshooting","purpose":"Clear the corrupted download cache that causes updates to hang.","config":["# Generate a readable update log","Get-WindowsUpdateLog -LogPath 'C:\\Temp\\WindowsUpdate.log'","","Get-Service wuauserv,bits,cryptsvc,msiserver |"," Select-Object Name,Status,StartType","","Stop-Service wuauserv,bits,cryptsvc -Force","","Rename-Item 'C:\\Windows\\SoftwareDistribution' 'SoftwareDistribution.old' -Force","Rename-Item 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\catroot2' 'catroot2.old' -Force","","Start-Service wuauserv,bits,cryptsvc","","# Force a fresh detection","(New-Object -ComObject Microsoft.Update.AutoUpdate).DetectNow()","","# Confirm what is installed","Get-HotFix | Sort-Object InstalledOn -Descending | Select-Object -First 10"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: SoftwareDistribution holds downloaded update content and catroot2 holds the signature catalogue. Renaming both with the services stopped forces Windows to rebuild them cleanly. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Deleting the folders while the services are running fails silently or leaves partial state, and the same symptom returns. The services must be stopped first. WHY IT MATTERS: Troubleshooting Windows Update is a stated AZ-802 objective."},{"id":66,"title":"Trace a connectivity and name resolution failure","level":"CORE","cat":"Troubleshooting","purpose":"Work down the layers from name to route to port in a few commands.","config":["# One command covering DNS, routing, and the TCP port","Test-NetConnection -ComputerName 'fileserver' -Port 445 -InformationLevel Detailed","","# Which resolver is the client using?","Get-DnsClientServerAddress -AddressFamily IPv4 |"," Select-Object InterfaceAlias,ServerAddresses","","# Query a specific server directly, bypassing the client cache","Resolve-DnsName 'fileserver.corp.contoso.com' -Server 10.1.1.10","","Get-DnsClientCache | Where-Object Entry -like '*fileserver*'","Clear-DnsClientCache","","Get-NetRoute -DestinationPrefix '0.0.0.0/0' |"," Select-Object NextHop,InterfaceAlias,RouteMetric"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: Test-NetConnection reports name resolution, the route taken, and whether the TCP port actually answers, which separates a DNS problem from a firewall problem in one step. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Testing only with ping proves nothing about the service — ICMP is frequently blocked while the application port is open, and vice versa. WHY IT MATTERS: Troubleshooting connectivity and name resolution are stated AZ-802 objectives."},{"id":67,"title":"Run dcdiag and interpret the failing tests","level":"INTER","cat":"Troubleshooting","purpose":"Get a comprehensive domain controller health report and target the failures.","config":["# Full health check on one DC","dcdiag /s:DC03 /v","","# Only the tests that matter most, across the enterprise","dcdiag /test:replications /test:advertising /test:fsmocheck `"," /test:services /test:dns /e","","# DNS-specific, with detail","dcdiag /test:dns /dnsall /s:DC03","","# Cross-check with the PowerShell equivalents","Get-ADReplicationFailure -Target DC03","Get-ADDomainController -Filter * |"," Select-Object Name,IsGlobalCatalog,OperationMasterRoles"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: dcdiag runs a battery of health tests and names each one as passed or failed, which narrows a vague 'AD is broken' report to a specific subsystem in one command. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Running dcdiag without /s or /e tests only the local DC, so a problem on a different domain controller is missed entirely. WHY IT MATTERS: Troubleshooting on-premises Active Directory is a stated AZ-802 objective, and dcdiag is the standard first tool."}]; // ---- Per-certificate lab configuration ---- // Every difference between the CCNA (Cisco IOS) lab and the Linux+ lab lives here, // so renderTerminalLab / wireLive / runScript / renderScriptSamples stay generic. window.SCRIPT_SAMPLES_SCOR = [{"id":1,"title":"IKEv2 Site-to-Site IPsec VPN","level":"CORE","cat":"VPN","purpose":"Build an IKEv2 route-based site-to-site IPsec tunnel with a virtual tunnel interface.","config":["! IOS XE hub-side IKEv2 VTI","crypto ikev2 proposal CORP-PROP"," encryption aes-gcm-256"," group 19","crypto ikev2 policy CORP-POL"," proposal CORP-PROP","crypto ikev2 keyring CORP-KR"," peer BRANCH1"," address 198.51.100.10"," pre-shared-key local C1sco123!"," pre-shared-key remote C1sco123!","crypto ikev2 profile CORP-PROF"," match identity remote address 198.51.100.10 255.255.255.255"," authentication local pre-share"," authentication remote pre-share"," keyring local CORP-KR","interface Tunnel100"," ip address 10.255.100.1 255.255.255.252"," tunnel source GigabitEthernet0/0"," tunnel destination 198.51.100.10"," tunnel protection ipsec profile CORP-IPSEC","crypto ipsec profile CORP-IPSEC"," set ikev2-profile CORP-PROF"," set transform-set ESP-GCM","crypto ipsec transform-set ESP-GCM esp-gcm 256"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: The IKEv2 proposal, keyring, profile, and IPsec profile provide matching negotiation and peer authentication for the VTI. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Omitting the remote identity match or attaching the wrong IPsec profile leaves the tunnel without a usable IKEv2 policy association. EXAM ANGLE: A VTI routes protected traffic by tunnel routing rather than a crypto-map ACL."},{"id":2,"title":"DMVPN Phase 3 Hub","level":"INTER","cat":"VPN","purpose":"Configure a DMVPN hub that accepts dynamic spoke registration and sends NHRP redirects.","config":["! IOS XE DMVPN Phase 3 hub","interface Tunnel0"," ip address 10.10.10.1 255.255.255.0"," no ip split-horizon eigrp 100"," ip nhrp network-id 100"," ip nhrp redirect"," ip nhrp map multicast dynamic"," tunnel source GigabitEthernet0/0"," tunnel mode gre multipoint"," tunnel key 100"," tunnel protection ipsec profile DMVPN-IPSEC","router eigrp 100"," network 10.10.10.0 0.0.0.255","crypto ipsec profile DMVPN-IPSEC"," set transform-set DMVPN-SET","crypto ipsec transform-set DMVPN-SET esp-aes 256 esp-sha-hmac"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: The multipoint GRE tunnel accepts dynamic NHRP mappings, while ip nhrp redirect enables Phase 3 shortcut signaling. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: A point-to-point GRE tunnel or a missing multicast map prevents dynamic spoke operation and routing protocol adjacencies. EXAM ANGLE: Phase 3 adds redirect and shortcut behavior so the hub can remain the routing next hop while data becomes direct."},{"id":3,"title":"ASA Static NAT and Outside HTTPS ACL","level":"CORE","cat":"Firewall","purpose":"Publish one inside HTTPS server with static NAT and an explicit inbound access rule.","config":["! ASA outside publication","object network WEB-SRV"," host 10.1.10.20"," nat (inside,outside) static 198.51.100.20","access-list OUTSIDE-IN extended permit tcp any object WEB-SRV eq https","access-group OUTSIDE-IN in interface outside","access-list INSIDE-OUT extended permit ip 10.1.10.0 255.255.255.0 any","access-group INSIDE-OUT in interface inside","policy-map global_policy"," class inspection_default"," inspect dns preset_dns_map","service-policy global_policy global"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: The object NAT creates a stable public mapping and the outside ACL independently authorizes TCP/443 to the real host. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: A static NAT rule alone does not permit inbound ASA traffic when an interface ACL is applied. EXAM ANGLE: ASA ACLs use real addresses in modern 8.3+ NAT configurations."},{"id":4,"title":"ASA Network Object Groups","level":"INTER","cat":"Firewall","purpose":"Use nested network and service object groups to simplify a partner access rule.","config":["! ASA object-group policy","object-group network APP-SERVERS"," network-object host 10.20.10.21"," network-object host 10.20.10.22","object-group network PARTNER-NETS"," network-object 203.0.113.0 255.255.255.0","object-group service APP-PORTS tcp"," port-object eq https"," port-object eq 8443","access-list OUTSIDE-IN extended permit tcp object-group PARTNER-NETS object-group APP-SERVERS object-group APP-PORTS","access-group OUTSIDE-IN in interface outside","logging enable","logging buffered warnings"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: Object groups compact repeated sources, destinations, and ports into a single maintainable ACE. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Defining a service object group without the tcp keyword or applying the ACL to the wrong interface does not match the intended flow. EXAM ANGLE: Nested objects improve readability but do not change ASA first-match ACL processing."},{"id":5,"title":"IOS XE Zone-Based Firewall","level":"CORE","cat":"Network Firewall","purpose":"Inspect inside-to-outside web and DNS traffic with a directional zone-pair policy.","config":["! IOS XE ZBFW","zone security INSIDE","zone security OUTSIDE","class-map type inspect match-any CM-WEB-DNS"," match protocol http"," match protocol https"," match protocol dns","policy-map type inspect PM-INSIDE-OUT"," class type inspect CM-WEB-DNS"," inspect"," class class-default"," drop log","zone-pair security ZP-INSIDE-OUT source INSIDE destination OUTSIDE"," service-policy type inspect PM-INSIDE-OUT","interface GigabitEthernet0/1"," zone-member security INSIDE","interface GigabitEthernet0/0"," zone-member security OUTSIDE"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: The zone pair binds a stateful policy to traffic from INSIDE to OUTSIDE and return traffic is allowed for inspected sessions. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Merely placing interfaces in zones without a zone-pair results in interzone traffic being denied. EXAM ANGLE: Pass is stateless whereas inspect builds state and allows return traffic."},{"id":6,"title":"802.1X with MAB Fallback","level":"CORE","cat":"Secure Access","purpose":"Enable dot1x authentication on an access port and fall back to MAB for non-supplicant devices.","config":["! IOS XE access port authentication","aaa new-model","aaa authentication dot1x default group radius","dot1x system-auth-control","interface GigabitEthernet1/0/10"," switchport mode access"," switchport access vlan 999"," authentication port-control auto"," authentication order dot1x mab"," authentication priority dot1x mab"," mab"," dot1x pae authenticator"," spanning-tree portfast"," spanning-tree bpduguard enable"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: The port tries 802.1X first and uses MAB only when the endpoint does not respond as a supplicant. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Setting the port force-authorized bypasses both 802.1X and MAB, defeating ISE policy enforcement. EXAM ANGLE: The authentication order controls the sequence and the priority selects the preferred successful method."},{"id":7,"title":"RADIUS and TACACS+ AAA","level":"CORE","cat":"Device Administration","purpose":"Use TACACS+ for administrator command authorization and RADIUS for network access authentication.","config":["! IOS XE AAA method lists","aaa new-model","tacacs server TAC1"," address ipv4 10.10.10.20"," key 0 C1scoTacacs!","radius server ISE1"," address ipv4 10.10.10.10 auth-port 1812 acct-port 1813"," key 0 C1scoRadius!","aaa group server tacacs+ ADMIN-TAC"," server name TAC1","aaa authentication login VTY group ADMIN-TAC local","aaa authorization exec VTY group ADMIN-TAC local if-authenticated","aaa authorization commands 15 VTY group ADMIN-TAC local","line vty 0 4"," login authentication VTY"," authorization commands 15 VTY"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: TACACS+ supports granular command authorization for device administrators, while RADIUS remains available for network access services. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Configuring a server object without referencing it in a group or method list does not send authentication requests there. EXAM ANGLE: TACACS+ encrypts the full payload and separates authentication, authorization, and accounting."},{"id":8,"title":"Control Plane Policing for Management Traffic","level":"INTER","cat":"Control Plane","purpose":"Protect the route processor by rate-limiting SSH and SNMP destined to the router.","config":["! IOS XE CoPP","ip access-list extended COPP-MGMT"," permit tcp any any eq 22"," permit udp any any eq snmp","class-map match-any CM-COPP-MGMT"," match access-group name COPP-MGMT","policy-map PM-COPP"," class CM-COPP-MGMT"," police 64000 conform-action transmit exceed-action drop"," class class-default"," police 320000 conform-action transmit exceed-action drop","control-plane"," service-policy input PM-COPP","logging buffered informational"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: CoPP applies the policy at the control plane so traffic addressed to the router CPU is constrained before it can exhaust processing resources. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Applying a service policy to a transit interface does not protect packets that terminate on the router itself. EXAM ANGLE: Classify critical protocols carefully; overly aggressive CoPP can drop legitimate routing or management traffic."},{"id":9,"title":"SNMPv3 AuthPriv Monitoring","level":"CORE","cat":"Management Security","purpose":"Configure an encrypted and authenticated SNMPv3 monitoring user with an ACL restriction.","config":["! IOS XE SNMPv3 authPriv","ip access-list standard NMS-SOURCES"," permit 10.50.50.10","snmp-server view MONITOR iso included","snmp-server group NMS v3 priv read MONITOR access NMS-SOURCES","snmp-server user nmsuser NMS v3 auth sha AuthPass123 priv aes 128 PrivPass123","snmp-server host 10.50.50.10 version 3 priv nmsuser","snmp-server enable traps snmp authentication linkdown linkup coldstart warmstart","snmp-server ifindex persist","logging host 10.50.50.10","logging trap warnings"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: SNMPv3 authPriv supplies both message authentication and encryption, and the standard ACL restricts permitted NMS sources. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: An SNMPv2c community string sends requests without per-user authentication or privacy. EXAM ANGLE: authNoPriv authenticates only; authPriv is the secure option for credentials and management data."},{"id":10,"title":"Flexible NetFlow Export to Secure Network Analytics","level":"CORE","cat":"Visibility","purpose":"Export IPv4 flow records with interface and timing fields to a NetFlow collector.","config":["! IOS XE Flexible NetFlow","flow record SNA-RECORD"," match ipv4 source address"," match ipv4 destination address"," match transport source-port"," match transport destination-port"," collect interface input"," collect interface output"," collect counter bytes long"," collect timestamp absolute first last","flow exporter SNA-EXPORTER"," destination 10.60.60.60"," source Loopback0"," transport udp 2055","flow monitor SNA-MONITOR"," record SNA-RECORD"," exporter SNA-EXPORTER","interface GigabitEthernet0/1"," ip flow monitor SNA-MONITOR input"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: The flow record defines fields, the exporter sends them to the collector, and the monitor binds both to the interface. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Defining a record and exporter without applying the monitor produces no exported telemetry. EXAM ANGLE: Input and output attachment affect which direction becomes the source in the collected record."},{"id":11,"title":"IOS XE Device Hardening Baseline","level":"CORE","cat":"Device Security","purpose":"Apply a concise management-plane hardening baseline for SSH-only administration.","config":["! IOS XE hardening baseline","service password-encryption","security passwords min-length 12","enable secret 9 StrongEnableSecret!","ip domain name corp.example","crypto key generate rsa modulus 2048","ip ssh version 2","ip ssh time-out 30","ip ssh authentication-retries 2","username netadmin privilege 15 secret 9 StrongAdminSecret!","login block-for 120 attempts 3 within 60","line vty 0 4"," transport input ssh"," exec-timeout 10 0"," login local","no ip http server","no ip http secure-server"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: SSHv2, local secret hashes, login throttling, and disabled HTTP reduce common management-plane exposure. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Leaving Telnet or the HTTP server enabled preserves cleartext or unnecessary management services. EXAM ANGLE: A crypto key and domain name are prerequisites for SSH key generation on IOS XE."},{"id":12,"title":"Unicast Reverse Path Forwarding","level":"INTER","cat":"Infrastructure Security","purpose":"Apply loose-mode uRPF on an untrusted Internet-facing interface where a default route is valid.","config":["! IOS XE uRPF loose mode","interface GigabitEthernet0/0"," description Internet-facing"," ip verify unicast source reachable-via any allow-default"," no ip redirects"," no ip proxy-arp","ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 198.51.100.1","ip route 10.0.0.0 255.0.0.0 Null0 250","ip cef","logging buffered warnings"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: Loose uRPF accepts a source when any route, including the permitted default route, exists in the FIB and helps reject obviously spoofed addresses. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Strict mode requires the best return path to use the same ingress interface, which can drop legitimate asymmetric traffic. EXAM ANGLE: Choose strict mode for symmetric designs and loose mode where paths are asymmetric."},{"id":13,"title":"DHCP Snooping and Dynamic ARP Inspection","level":"CORE","cat":"Layer 2 Security","purpose":"Trust the uplink DHCP server path and validate ARP bindings for user VLANs.","config":["! IOS XE DHCP snooping and DAI","ip dhcp snooping","ip dhcp snooping vlan 10,20","ip dhcp snooping database flash:dhcp_snoop.db","ip arp inspection vlan 10,20","ip arp inspection validate src-mac dst-mac ip","interface GigabitEthernet1/0/48"," description Uplink-to-distribution"," ip dhcp snooping trust"," ip arp inspection trust","interface range GigabitEthernet1/0/1-24"," ip dhcp snooping limit rate 15"," spanning-tree portfast"," spanning-tree bpduguard enable"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: DHCP snooping builds trusted bindings from legitimate DHCP replies, and DAI validates untrusted ARP against those bindings. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Trusting user-facing ports permits rogue DHCP replies and spoofed ARP messages to bypass the controls. EXAM ANGLE: DAI depends on snooping bindings unless static ARP inspection ACLs are configured."},{"id":14,"title":"Access Port Security","level":"CORE","cat":"Layer 2 Security","purpose":"Limit a user access port to two sticky secure MAC addresses and shut it on violation.","config":["! IOS XE port security","interface GigabitEthernet1/0/12"," description Finance workstation"," switchport mode access"," switchport access vlan 30"," switchport port-security"," switchport port-security maximum 2"," switchport port-security mac-address sticky"," switchport port-security violation shutdown"," switchport port-security aging time 60"," switchport port-security aging type inactivity"," spanning-tree portfast"," spanning-tree bpduguard enable","no shutdown"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: Sticky learning stores observed secure MAC addresses in the running configuration and a shutdown violation disables the port on an unauthorized source. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Port security does not operate on a dynamically negotiated trunk and should be used on a static access interface. EXAM ANGLE: Restrict, protect, and shutdown have different violation visibility and recovery behavior."},{"id":15,"title":"MACsec on an Access Uplink","level":"ADV","cat":"Link Encryption","purpose":"Enable MKA-based MACsec on a compatible point-to-point Ethernet link.","config":["! IOS XE MACsec peer configuration","mka policy MACSEC-POLICY"," key-server priority 10"," macsec-cipher-suite gcm-aes-256","interface GigabitEthernet1/0/48"," description Protected-switch-uplink"," switchport mode trunk"," mka policy MACSEC-POLICY"," mka pre-shared-key key-chain MACSEC-KEYS"," macsec network-link","key chain MACSEC-KEYS macsec"," key 1"," key-string 0 C1scoMacsecKey!"," cryptographic-algorithm hmac-sha-256"," lifetime local 00:00:00 Jan 1 2026 infinite"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: MKA authenticates link peers and derives secure associations that MACsec uses to encrypt Ethernet frames on that hop. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: MACsec configuration on only one endpoint cannot form an MKA session or protected channel. EXAM ANGLE: MACsec is hop by hop at Layer 2, unlike IPsec which can protect routed Layer 3 traffic."},{"id":16,"title":"ERSPAN Remote Packet Capture","level":"INTER","cat":"Visibility","purpose":"Mirror selected ingress traffic into a GRE ERSPAN session for remote analysis.","config":["! IOS XE ERSPAN source session","monitor session 1 type erspan-source"," source interface GigabitEthernet1/0/10 rx"," destination"," erspan-id 101"," ip address 192.0.2.50"," origin ip address 192.0.2.10"," vrf Mgmt-vrf","monitor session 1 type erspan-source"," filter vlan 30","interface GigabitEthernet1/0/10"," description Suspect-endpoint-port"," switchport access vlan 30","ip route vrf Mgmt-vrf 192.0.2.50 255.255.255.255 10.0.0.1","logging buffered informational"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: ERSPAN encapsulates mirrored packets in GRE and sends them to a remote analyzer, unlike local SPAN which needs a directly connected destination port. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: A missing route in the ERSPAN VRF prevents the mirrored GRE packets from reaching the collector. EXAM ANGLE: SPAN observes local interfaces; ERSPAN extends the observation point across Layer 3."},{"id":17,"title":"GETVPN Group Member","level":"ADV","cat":"VPN","purpose":"Configure a GETVPN group member to obtain group policy and keys from redundant key servers.","config":["! IOS XE GETVPN group member","crypto isakmp policy 10"," encr aes 256"," hash sha256"," authentication pre-share"," group 19","crypto isakmp key C1scoGDOIKey address 203.0.113.10","crypto gdoi group CORP-GDOI"," identity number 1001"," server address ipv4 203.0.113.10"," server address ipv4 203.0.113.11","crypto map GETVPN-MAP 10 gdoi"," set group CORP-GDOI","interface GigabitEthernet0/1"," crypto map GETVPN-MAP","ip access-list extended GDOI-INTERESTING"," permit ip 10.0.0.0 0.255.255.255 10.0.0.0 0.255.255.255"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: A GETVPN group member registers to a key server and receives a common group policy and traffic-encryption keys for private-WAN encryption. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: GETVPN is not a tunnel overlay, so expecting NHRP or tunnel interfaces would be a design mismatch. EXAM ANGLE: GETVPN preserves original IP headers and is suited to routed private transports with any-to-any communication."},{"id":18,"title":"FTD Threat Defense Manager Registration","level":"INTER","cat":"Secure Firewall","purpose":"Register an FTD appliance to FMC for centralized policy and event management.","config":["! FTD CLI registration","configure network ipv4 manual 10.70.70.20 255.255.255.0 10.70.70.1","configure manager add 10.70.70.10 FMC_REG_KEY","show managers","show network","exit","! Accept the device in FMC","! Deploy an access-control policy from FMC","! Verify registration before production cutover"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: The registration key binds the FTD to the FMC management plane so centralized access control and event configuration can be deployed. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Reachability alone does not register a device; the manager address and shared registration key must match. EXAM ANGLE: FMC manages policy while the FTD appliance performs the data-plane inspection."},{"id":19,"title":"Cisco Umbrella DNS Forwarder","level":"INTER","cat":"DNS Security","purpose":"Forward enterprise DNS queries to Umbrella resolvers while preserving local internal resolution.","config":["! IOS XE DNS forwarder","ip domain lookup","ip name-server 208.67.222.222","ip name-server 208.67.220.220","ip dns server","ip dns primary corp.example soa ns.corp.example admin.corp.example 3600 600 86400 60","ip host files flash:hosts.txt","ip access-list standard DNS-CLIENTS"," permit 10.40.0.0 0.0.255.255","ip dns view default"," domain timeout 2"," domain retry 1","interface GigabitEthernet0/1"," ip helper-address 10.40.40.10","logging host 10.70.70.70"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: The router can provide local forwarding while forwarding unresolved external queries to the Umbrella recursive resolvers for DNS-layer policy. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Pointing endpoints directly to arbitrary public resolvers bypasses the enterprise identity and policy path. EXAM ANGLE: Umbrella DNS security is an early destination control and is not a replacement for HTTPS content inspection."},{"id":20,"title":"TrustSec SXP Speaker Binding","level":"ADV","cat":"TrustSec","purpose":"Configure an SXP speaker to publish IP-to-SGT bindings toward an enforcement-capable peer.","config":["! IOS XE TrustSec SXP speaker","cts role-based enforcement","cts authorization list CTS-AUTH","cts sxp enable","cts sxp default source-ip 10.80.80.1","cts sxp default password 0 C1scoSXPKey!","cts sxp connection peer 10.80.80.2 password default mode speaker","cts sxp connection peer 10.80.80.2 source 10.80.80.1","cts role-based permissions from 10 to 20"," permit tcp dst eq 443","cts role-based sgt-map 10.30.30.0/24 sgt 10","interface GigabitEthernet0/1"," cts manual"," policy static sgt 10 trusted"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: SXP distributes IP-to-SGT bindings from the speaker to a listener when inline TrustSec tagging is not available across the path. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: An SXP peer configured on only one side or with mismatched passwords cannot establish a binding exchange. EXAM ANGLE: SXP propagates bindings; it does not carry tags in the packet data plane."},{"id":21,"title":"ISE RADIUS Dynamic Authorization","level":"INTER","cat":"Secure Access","purpose":"Accept ISE Change of Authorization requests so it can reauthorize a live authenticated switchport session.","config":["! IOS XE ISE CoA support","aaa new-model","radius server ISE1"," address ipv4 10.10.10.10 auth-port 1812 acct-port 1813"," key 0 C1scoRadius!","aaa group server radius ISE-GROUP"," server name ISE1","aaa authentication dot1x default group ISE-GROUP","aaa authorization network default group ISE-GROUP","aaa accounting dot1x default start-stop group ISE-GROUP","aaa server radius dynamic-author"," client 10.10.10.10 server-key 0 C1scoRadius!"," auth-type any","interface GigabitEthernet1/0/10"," authentication port-control auto"," dot1x pae authenticator"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: The dynamic-author section permits ISE to issue CoA or disconnect messages that force a new authorization decision for an existing session. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Accounting alone reports session state but does not authorize the RADIUS server to alter that session. EXAM ANGLE: CoA is central to posture change, guest CWA completion, and other mid-session policy updates."},{"id":22,"title":"FlexVPN IKEv2 Remote Access Profile","level":"ADV","cat":"VPN","purpose":"Build an IKEv2 FlexVPN virtual-template policy for authenticated remote-access clients.","config":["! IOS XE FlexVPN server","crypto ikev2 authorization policy FLEX-AUTHZ"," pool FLEX-POOL"," dns 10.1.1.53"," route set access-list FLEX-SPLIT","crypto ikev2 profile FLEX-SERVER"," match identity remote any"," authentication local rsa-sig"," authentication remote eap query-identity"," pki trustpoint VPN-TP"," aaa authentication eap FLEX-EAP"," aaa authorization group eap list FLEX-AUTHZ FLEX-AUTHZ"," virtual-template 1 mode auto","interface Virtual-Template1 type tunnel"," ip unnumbered Loopback0"," tunnel mode ipsec ipv4"," tunnel protection ipsec profile FLEX-IPSEC","ip local pool FLEX-POOL 10.250.10.1 10.250.10.100","ip access-list standard FLEX-SPLIT"," permit 10.0.0.0 0.255.255.255"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: The IKEv2 profile accepts EAP-authenticated peers and instantiates a protected virtual-access interface from the virtual template. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Without an authorization policy and address pool, a client can authenticate but cannot receive usable network parameters. EXAM ANGLE: FlexVPN is a modular IKEv2 framework that supports both site and remote-access designs."},{"id":23,"title":"ASA AnyConnect Group Policy","level":"INTER","cat":"Remote Access","purpose":"Create a remote-access group policy that applies split tunneling and a client address pool.","config":["! ASA AnyConnect policy","ip local pool AC-POOL 10.250.20.1-10.250.20.100 mask 255.255.255.0","access-list AC-SPLIT standard permit 10.0.0.0 255.0.0.0","group-policy AC-GP internal","group-policy AC-GP attributes"," vpn-tunnel-protocol ssl-client ikev2"," split-tunnel-policy tunnelspecified"," split-tunnel-network-list value AC-SPLIT"," dns-server value 10.1.1.53"," default-domain value corp.example","tunnel-group AC-PROFILE type remote-access","tunnel-group AC-PROFILE general-attributes"," address-pool AC-POOL"," default-group-policy AC-GP","tunnel-group AC-PROFILE webvpn-attributes"," group-alias Corp-Remote enable"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: The tunnel group supplies the connection profile and address pool, while the group policy supplies user-session controls such as split tunneling and DNS. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Defining a split ACL without referencing it from the group policy leaves the client with the default tunnel behavior. EXAM ANGLE: Tunnel groups identify connection profiles; group policies determine permissions and client behavior."},{"id":24,"title":"ASA Active Standby Stateful Failover","level":"ADV","cat":"High Availability","purpose":"Configure an ASA pair for active/standby failover with dedicated failover and state links.","config":["! ASA primary unit","failover","failover lan unit primary","failover lan interface FO_LINK GigabitEthernet0/2","failover link STATE_LINK GigabitEthernet0/3","failover interface ip FO_LINK 169.254.1.1 255.255.255.252 standby 169.254.1.2","failover interface ip STATE_LINK 169.254.2.1 255.255.255.252 standby 169.254.2.2","failover key C1scoFailoverKey!","failover replication http","monitor-interface inside","monitor-interface outside","interface GigabitEthernet0/0"," nameif outside"," security-level 0"," ip address 198.51.100.2 255.255.255.0 standby 198.51.100.3","interface GigabitEthernet0/1"," nameif inside"," security-level 100"," ip address 10.1.10.1 255.255.255.0 standby 10.1.10.2","write memory"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: Dedicated failover and state links synchronize health, configuration, and connection state so the standby can assume forwarding with minimal disruption. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Using only a failover link without a state link yields less capable stateless recovery for established connections. EXAM ANGLE: Monitor interfaces determine path health and stateful failover replicates connection and translation information."}]; window.SCRIPT_SAMPLES_DCCOR = [{"id":1,"title":"vPC Domain and Peer-Link","level":"CORE","cat":"Network","purpose":"Builds a resilient Nexus vPC domain and peer-link.","config":["feature lacp","feature vpc","vpc domain 10"," peer-keepalive destination 192.0.2.2 source 192.0.2.1 vrf management"," peer-switch","interface port-channel1"," switchport mode trunk"," switchport trunk allowed vlan 10,20,30"," vpc peer-link","interface ethernet1/1"," channel-group 1 mode active"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: vPC needs a common domain, an independent keepalive path, and a peer-link that carries every required VLAN. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: A missing dependent feature, matching interface setting, or policy association leaves this workflow incomplete. EXAM ANGLE: Confirm the control-plane state first, then use the relevant show command to verify forwarding or policy effect."},{"id":2,"title":"vPC Member Port-Channel","level":"CORE","cat":"Network","purpose":"Creates a dual-homed downstream server vPC.","config":["feature lacp","interface port-channel10"," switchport mode trunk"," switchport trunk allowed vlan 10,20"," spanning-tree port type edge trunk"," vpc 10","interface ethernet1/10"," channel-group 10 mode active","interface ethernet1/11"," channel-group 10 mode active"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: The vpc statement binds the downstream LAG to the configured vPC domain. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: A missing dependent feature, matching interface setting, or policy association leaves this workflow incomplete. EXAM ANGLE: Confirm the control-plane state first, then use the relevant show command to verify forwarding or policy effect."},{"id":3,"title":"OSPF Underlay Leaf","level":"CORE","cat":"Network","purpose":"Configures a routed OSPF fabric underlay.","config":["feature ospf","interface loopback0"," ip address 10.255.0.11/32"," ip router ospf UNDERLAY area 0.0.0.0","interface ethernet1/49"," no switchport"," ip address 10.0.1.0/31"," ip ospf network point-to-point"," ip router ospf UNDERLAY area 0.0.0.0","router ospf UNDERLAY"," router-id 10.255.0.11"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: The loopback is a stable fabric identity and the point-to-point link forms the routed transport. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: A missing dependent feature, matching interface setting, or policy association leaves this workflow incomplete. EXAM ANGLE: Confirm the control-plane state first, then use the relevant show command to verify forwarding or policy effect."},{"id":4,"title":"eBGP Underlay Leaf","level":"CORE","cat":"Network","purpose":"Builds an eBGP underlay session to a spine.","config":["feature bgp","interface ethernet1/49"," no switchport"," ip address 10.0.1.0/31","router bgp 65101"," router-id 10.255.0.11"," neighbor 10.0.1.1 remote-as 65000"," address-family ipv4 unicast"," network 10.255.0.11/32"," neighbor 10.0.1.1 address-family ipv4 unicast"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: The leaf advertises its loopback through eBGP so remote VTEPs can resolve its address. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: A missing dependent feature, matching interface setting, or policy association leaves this workflow incomplete. EXAM ANGLE: Confirm the control-plane state first, then use the relevant show command to verify forwarding or policy effect."},{"id":5,"title":"VXLAN EVPN Feature Base","level":"CORE","cat":"Network","purpose":"Enables VXLAN and EVPN functions on a leaf.","config":["feature nv overlay","feature vn-segment-vlan-based","feature bgp","feature pim","nv overlay evpn","router bgp 65101"," address-family l2vpn evpn"," retain route-target all"," neighbor 10.255.0.1 remote-as 65000"," update-source loopback0"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: NV overlay enables NVE operation and the L2VPN EVPN address family distributes overlay reachability. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: A missing dependent feature, matching interface setting, or policy association leaves this workflow incomplete. EXAM ANGLE: Confirm the control-plane state first, then use the relevant show command to verify forwarding or policy effect."},{"id":6,"title":"NVE Interface and L2 VNI","level":"CORE","cat":"Network","purpose":"Maps a VLAN to an NVE member VNI with ingress replication.","config":["feature nv overlay","interface loopback1"," ip address 10.255.1.11/32","vlan 100"," vn-segment 10100","interface nve1"," no shutdown"," host-reachability protocol bgp"," source-interface loopback1"," member vni 10100"," ingress-replication protocol bgp"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: The NVE source loopback is the VTEP address and BGP EVPN provides the replication membership. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: A missing dependent feature, matching interface setting, or policy association leaves this workflow incomplete. EXAM ANGLE: Confirm the control-plane state first, then use the relevant show command to verify forwarding or policy effect."},{"id":7,"title":"Anycast Gateway SVI","level":"CORE","cat":"Network","purpose":"Builds an anycast VXLAN default gateway.","config":["feature interface-vlan","fabric forwarding anycast-gateway-mac 0000.2222.3333","vlan 100"," vn-segment 10100","interface vlan100"," no shutdown"," vrf member BLUE"," ip address 192.168.100.1/24"," fabric forwarding mode anycast-gateway","interface nve1"," member vni 10100"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: The shared SVI IP and anycast MAC keep first-hop routing on the ingress leaf. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: A missing dependent feature, matching interface setting, or policy association leaves this workflow incomplete. EXAM ANGLE: Confirm the control-plane state first, then use the relevant show command to verify forwarding or policy effect."},{"id":8,"title":"Tenant VRF and L3 VNI","level":"CORE","cat":"Network","purpose":"Associates a tenant VRF with an L3 VNI.","config":["vrf context BLUE"," vni 50000"," rd auto"," address-family ipv4 unicast"," route-target both auto","vlan 500"," vn-segment 50000","interface vlan500"," no shutdown"," vrf member BLUE"," ip forward","interface nve1"," member vni 50000 associate-vrf"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: The VRF VNI and NVE association identify routed tenant traffic in the overlay. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: A missing dependent feature, matching interface setting, or policy association leaves this workflow incomplete. EXAM ANGLE: Confirm the control-plane state first, then use the relevant show command to verify forwarding or policy effect."},{"id":9,"title":"FC VSAN and Host F-Port","level":"CORE","cat":"Storage","purpose":"Creates VSAN 10 and assigns a host-facing FC port.","config":["feature npiv","vsan database"," vsan 10 name PROD_SAN","interface fc1/1"," no shutdown"," switchport mode F"," switchport trunk mode off"," switchport vsan 10","fcdomain fcid database 0x010000 0x01ffff vsan 10","fcdomain domain 10 static vsan 10"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: The F-Port joins a host to VSAN 10 so fabric login, FCID assignment, and zoning can occur. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: A missing dependent feature, matching interface setting, or policy association leaves this workflow incomplete. EXAM ANGLE: Confirm the control-plane state first, then use the relevant show command to verify forwarding or policy effect."},{"id":10,"title":"FC Zone and Active Zoneset","level":"ADV","cat":"Storage","purpose":"Creates single-initiator zoning and activates it.","config":["device-alias database"," device-alias name APP1_HBA pwwn 20:00:00:25:b5:01:01:01"," device-alias name ARRAY_A pwwn 50:00:09:73:00:10:00:01","device-alias commit","zone name APP1_ARRAYA vsan 10"," member device-alias APP1_HBA"," member device-alias ARRAY_A","zoneset name PROD_ZS vsan 10"," member APP1_ARRAYA","zoneset activate name PROD_ZS vsan 10"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: An active zoneset applies the WWPN visibility policy within the specified VSAN. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: A missing dependent feature, matching interface setting, or policy association leaves this workflow incomplete. EXAM ANGLE: Confirm the control-plane state first, then use the relevant show command to verify forwarding or policy effect."},{"id":11,"title":"VSAN Trunking over ISL","level":"INTER","cat":"Storage","purpose":"Carries only approved VSANs over an FC ISL.","config":["interface fc1/48"," no shutdown"," switchport mode E"," switchport trunk mode on"," switchport trunk allowed vsan 10,20,30"," channel-group 48 force","interface port-channel48"," switchport mode E"," switchport trunk mode on"," switchport trunk allowed vsan 10,20,30"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: The E-Port trunk extends selected VSANs and port-channeling provides resilient inter-switch transport. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: A missing dependent feature, matching interface setting, or policy association leaves this workflow incomplete.
