WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Broad matching or a missing alternate target can select the wrong peer or leave no recovery path. EXAM ANGLE: Distinguish inbound matching, outbound routing, and shared policy application."}]; window.SCRIPT_SAMPLES_AUTOCOR = [{"id":1,"title":"Python REST client with bearer token and bounded retry","level":"CORE","cat":"Python REST","purpose":"Call a controller API with a scoped bearer token and controlled retries for transient responses.","config":["# pip install requests","import os","import requests","from requests.adapters import HTTPAdapter","from urllib3.util.retry import Retry","token = os.environ['CONTROLLER_TOKEN']","base = os.environ['CONTROLLER_URL'].rstrip('/')","retry = Retry(total=3, backoff_factor=0.5, status_forcelist=[429, 500, 502, 503, 504], allowed_methods=['GET'])","session = requests.Session()","session.mount('https://', HTTPAdapter(max_retries=retry))","headers = {'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + token, 'Accept': 'application/json'}","response = session.get(base + '/api/v1/devices', headers=headers, timeout=20)","response.raise_for_status()","print(response.json())"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: the bearer token is sent in the Authorization header and Retry only retries idempotent GET requests for transient status codes. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: an unbounded loop can overload a rate-limited controller and retrying a POST can duplicate a change. EXAM ANGLE: use timeouts, raise_for_status, and bounded exponential backoff in production clients."},{"id":2,"title":"Python cursor pagination loop","level":"CORE","cat":"Python REST","purpose":"Collect every page from a cursor-based inventory endpoint without assuming an offset scheme.","config":["# pip install requests","import os","import requests","url = os.environ['INVENTORY_URL']","headers = {'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + os.environ['CONTROLLER_TOKEN']}","devices = []","while url:"," reply = requests.get(url, headers=headers, timeout=20)"," reply.raise_for_status()"," body = reply.json()"," devices.extend(body['items'])"," url = body.get('next')","print('collected', len(devices), 'devices')","for device in devices:"," print(device['id'], device.get('name', 'unnamed'))"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: the client treats the next cursor URI as opaque and stops only when the API omits it. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: incrementing a guessed offset can skip or duplicate objects when the API uses cursors. EXAM ANGLE: pagination belongs in the client loop, not in a one-time GET."},{"id":3,"title":"Meraki Dashboard organization networks call","level":"CORE","cat":"Meraki API","purpose":"List networks in a Meraki organization by using the Dashboard v1 API key header.","config":["# pip install requests","import os","import requests","api_key = os.environ['MERAKI_DASHBOARD_API_KEY']","org_id = os.environ['MERAKI_ORG_ID']","url = 'https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/organizations/' + org_id + '/networks'","headers = {'X-Cisco-Meraki-API-Key': api_key, 'Accept': 'application/json'}","response = requests.get(url, headers=headers, timeout=30)","response.raise_for_status()","for network in response.json():"," print(network['id'], network['name'], network['productTypes'])","# store secrets outside source control","# inspect response headers for rate-limit information"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: the Dashboard API accepts X-Cisco-Meraki-API-Key and returns organization network objects from the v1 resource path. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: placing the key in a URL exposes it to logs and browser history. EXAM ANGLE: Meraki is cloud-managed, so calls go to Dashboard rather than directly to an on-premises device."},{"id":4,"title":"Catalyst Center device inventory call","level":"CORE","cat":"Catalyst Center API","purpose":"Authenticate to Catalyst Center and request the current network-device inventory.","config":["# pip install requests","import os","import requests","base = os.environ['CATALYST_CENTER_URL'].rstrip('/')","user = os.environ['CATALYST_CENTER_USER']","password = os.environ['CATALYST_CENTER_PASSWORD']","token_reply = requests.post(base + '/dna/system/api/v1/auth/token', auth=(user, password), timeout=20, verify=False)","token_reply.raise_for_status()","token = token_reply.json()['Token']","headers = {'X-Auth-Token': token, 'Accept': 'application/json'}","reply = requests.get(base + '/dna/intent/api/v1/network-device', headers=headers, timeout=30, verify=False)","reply.raise_for_status()","for device in reply.json()['response']:"," print(device['hostname'], device.get('managementIpAddress'))"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: the authentication endpoint returns a token that is passed as X-Auth-Token to Intent API calls. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: using Basic authentication for the inventory request bypasses the normal token workflow and may be rejected. EXAM ANGLE: in production, replace verify=False with a trusted CA bundle and protect account credentials."},{"id":5,"title":"RESTCONF curl read of an IOS XE interface","level":"CORE","cat":"RESTCONF","purpose":"Retrieve a keyed IOS XE native interface through the RESTCONF data resource.","config":["# set IOSXE_HOST and IOSXE_USER before running","export IOSXE_HOST=192.0.2.10","export IOSXE_USER=netops","read -s IOSXE_PASSWORD","# RESTCONF over HTTPS uses YANG-modeled paths","curl --fail --silent --show-error --insecure --user \"${IOSXE_USER}:${IOSXE_PASSWORD}\" --header \"Accept: application/yang-data+json\" \"https://${IOSXE_HOST}/restconf/data/Cisco-IOS-XE-native:native/interface/GigabitEthernet=GigabitEthernet1\" | python -m json.tool","# use a trusted CA instead of --insecure in production","# use GET for read-only retrieval","# keys select a specific YANG list instance"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: the URI walks the native YANG tree and selects one list entry with its GigabitEthernet key. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: a CLI-style path or unkeyed list URI does not identify the modeled resource. EXAM ANGLE: RESTCONF uses HTTPS plus HTTP methods and YANG-data media types."},{"id":6,"title":"Ansible YAML inventory for IOS XE","level":"CORE","cat":"Ansible","purpose":"Define an IOS XE device group with network CLI connection variables.","config":["# inventory.yml","all:"," children:"," iosxe:"," hosts:"," edge1:"," ansible_host: 192.0.2.10"," vars:"," ansible_connection: ansible.netcommon.network_cli"," ansible_network_os: cisco.ios.ios"," ansible_user: netops"," ansible_password: \"{{ vault_iosxe_password }}\""," ansible_become: true"," ansible_become_method: enable"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: inventory variables select the network_cli transport and IOS platform collection for all iosxe hosts. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: generic SSH lacks the network platform behavior many network modules require. EXAM ANGLE: keep passwords in Ansible Vault or another secret store rather than literal inventory values."},{"id":7,"title":"Ansible idempotent interface playbook","level":"CORE","cat":"Ansible","purpose":"Apply an interface description with the IOS configuration module.","config":["# site.yml","---","- name: Configure branch edge interface"," hosts: iosxe"," gather_facts: false"," collections:"," - cisco.ios"," tasks:"," - name: Set routed uplink description"," cisco.ios.ios_config:"," parents: interface GigabitEthernet1"," lines:"," - description Uplink_to_WAN"," register: result"," - ansible.builtin.debug:"," var: result.changed"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: ios_config applies the intended line under the correct parent context and reports whether a change occurred. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: a raw CLI command may replay blindly and cannot reliably report convergence. EXAM ANGLE: network modules plus parent context make playbooks safer and more idempotent."},{"id":8,"title":"Ansible role task structure","level":"CORE","cat":"Ansible","purpose":"Package an interface baseline as a reusable role task file and invoke it from a play.","config":["# roles/interface_baseline/tasks/main.yml","---","- name: Set access interface description"," cisco.ios.ios_config:"," parents: \"interface {{ interface_name }}\""," lines:"," - \"description {{ interface_description }}\"","- name: Save only when configuration changed"," cisco.ios.ios_config:"," save_when: modified","# site.yml includes roles:","- hosts: iosxe"," roles:"," - role: interface_baseline"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: the role turns a repeated interface task into a parameterized unit that can be reused by multiple plays. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: duplicating tasks in each play makes intent and maintenance drift across sites. EXAM ANGLE: roles conventionally place primary tasks in roles//tasks/main.yml."},{"id":9,"title":"Terraform provider and local artifact resource","level":"CORE","cat":"Terraform","purpose":"Initialize a Terraform project that renders an approved network configuration artifact.","config":["# main.tf","terraform {"," required_providers {"," local = { source = \"hashicorp/local\", version = \"2.5.1\" }"," }","}","provider \"local\" {}","variable \"site_name\" { type = string }","resource \"local_file\" \"device_banner\" {"," filename = \"${path.module}/rendered/banner.txt\""," content = \"Authorized network: ${var.site_name}\\n\"","}","output \"banner_path\" { value = local_file.device_banner.filename }"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: required_providers pins the provider and local_file demonstrates Terraform resource declaration, interpolation, and output. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: unpinned providers can change behavior between pipeline runs. EXAM ANGLE: Terraform describes desired state and uses providers to reconcile it with a target API or system."},{"id":10,"title":"Git feature branch workflow","level":"CORE","cat":"Git","purpose":"Create a small reviewable automation change and prepare it for a pull request.","config":["# start from an up-to-date protected main branch","git switch main","git pull --ff-only origin main","git switch -c feature/branch-interface-description","# edit playbooks/interface.yml and run local checks","ansible-lint playbooks/interface.yml","git add playbooks/interface.yml","git commit -m \"Configure branch uplink description\"","git push -u origin feature/branch-interface-description","# open a pull request and wait for required checks","# merge only after review and approval","# delete the feature branch after merge","git switch main"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: the feature branch isolates one change and the pull request provides a review and testing gate before main changes. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: direct pushes to main bypass protected-branch controls and obscure peer review. EXAM ANGLE: a commit SHA is the durable link between code review and deployment evidence."},{"id":11,"title":"NETCONF get-config with ncclient","level":"INTER","cat":"NETCONF","purpose":"Read an IOS XE interface configuration subtree from the running datastore.","config":["# pip install ncclient","import os","from ncclient import manager","filter_xml = 'GigabitEthernet1'","with manager.connect(host=os.environ['IOSXE_HOST'], port=830, username=os.environ['IOSXE_USER'], password=os.environ['IOSXE_PASSWORD'], hostkey_verify=False, device_params={'name': 'iosxe'}) as m:"," reply = m.get_config(source='running', filter=('subtree', filter_xml))"," print(reply.xml)","# port 830 carries the NETCONF SSH subsystem","# use known-host verification in production","# select a filter namespace that matches the target model"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: ncclient establishes the NETCONF SSH session and get_config reads configuration from the named running datastore. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: a get operation may include operational state when the task requires configuration only. EXAM ANGLE: subtree filters reduce returned data and namespaces must match the YANG model."},{"id":12,"title":"NETCONF edit-config with ncclient","level":"INTER","cat":"NETCONF","purpose":"Set an interface description with an XML configuration payload and validate the RPC result.","config":["# pip install ncclient","import os","from ncclient import manager","payload = '1Uplink_to_WAN'","with manager.connect(host=os.environ['IOSXE_HOST'], port=830, username=os.environ['IOSXE_USER'], password=os.environ['IOSXE_PASSWORD'], hostkey_verify=False, device_params={'name': 'iosxe'}) as m:"," reply = m.edit_config(target='running', config=payload)"," if not reply.ok:"," raise RuntimeError(reply.xml)"," print('interface description configured')","# test against a lab device before production","# use candidate plus validate and commit when supported","# record the reply XML in the change log"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: edit_config carries a YANG-modeled config element to the target datastore and reply.ok confirms a successful RPC. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: sending CLI text or XML in the wrong namespace cannot be validated against the device schema. EXAM ANGLE: candidate, validate, and commit are capabilities to discover rather than assume."},{"id":13,"title":"RESTCONF Python PATCH with ETag guard","level":"INTER","cat":"RESTCONF","purpose":"Update an interface description only if the resource version has not changed since it was read.","config":["# pip install requests","import os","import requests","base = 'https://' + os.environ['IOSXE_HOST'] + '/restconf/data'","path = '/Cisco-IOS-XE-native:native/interface/GigabitEthernet=GigabitEthernet1'","auth = (os.environ['IOSXE_USER'], os.environ['IOSXE_PASSWORD'])","headers = {'Accept': 'application/yang-data+json'}","before = requests.get(base + path, auth=auth, headers=headers, verify=False, timeout=20)","before.raise_for_status()","headers['Content-Type'] = 'application/yang-data+json'","headers['If-Match'] = before.headers.get('ETag', '*')","payload = {'GigabitEthernet': {'name': 'GigabitEthernet1', 'description': 'Uplink_to_WAN'}}","after = requests.patch(base + path, auth=auth, headers=headers, json=payload, verify=False, timeout=20)","after.raise_for_status()","print(after.status_code)"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: the client reads the resource, sends a YANG JSON payload, and uses If-Match to protect against overwriting a newer version when ETags are supported. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: blind PATCH can overwrite another operator change between read and write. EXAM ANGLE: HTTP conditional headers are a concurrency control pattern for REST APIs."},{"id":14,"title":"Terraform controlled plan and state commands","level":"INTER","cat":"Terraform","purpose":"Format, validate, save a plan, apply that exact plan, and inspect state.","config":["# run from the Terraform root module","terraform init","terraform fmt -check -recursive","terraform validate","terraform plan -out=network.tfplan","terraform show network.tfplan","# approve the reviewed saved plan in CI","terraform apply network.tfplan","terraform state list","terraform state show local_file.device_banner","# do not edit terraform.tfstate by hand","# use terraform import for pre-existing managed objects","# store state remotely for team workflows"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: a saved plan ensures apply executes the reviewed action graph instead of recalculating a new proposal. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: applying without plan review can accept a surprising destroy or replacement. EXAM ANGLE: state commands inspect Terraform bindings; configuration changes should be made in HCL, not by manually editing state."},{"id":15,"title":"Terraform remote backend with locking","level":"INTER","cat":"Terraform","purpose":"Configure an S3 backend and DynamoDB lock table for shared state coordination.","config":["# backend.tf","terraform {"," backend \"s3\" {"," bucket = \"network-automation-tfstate\""," key = \"prod/branch.tfstate\""," region = \"us-east-1\""," encrypt = true"," dynamodb_table = \"network-automation-locks\""," }","}","# initialize or migrate state after backend changes","terraform init -migrate-state","# grant CI least-privilege access to state and lock resources"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: the remote backend gives the team one state location and DynamoDB provides a lock during plan and apply operations. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: each engineer holding local state can create conflicting resource decisions. EXAM ANGLE: state may contain sensitive values, so encrypt it and restrict backend access."},{"id":16,"title":"Dockerfile for an automation API client","level":"INTER","cat":"Containers","purpose":"Build a small non-root container image for a Python network automation service.","config":["# Dockerfile","FROM python:3.12-slim@sha256:replace-with-approved-digest","WORKDIR /app","RUN useradd --create-home --uid 10001 appuser","COPY requirements.txt .","RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt","COPY app.py .","USER appuser","ENV PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1","ENV PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1","CMD [\"python\", \"app.py\"]","# build with a pinned base digest","# pass tokens at runtime, never with COPY"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: dependency installation is cached before application code, the process runs as a non-root user, and the command is explicit. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: embedding tokens in an image layer exposes them to anyone who can inspect or pull the image. EXAM ANGLE: an image is immutable; environment-specific secrets belong at runtime."},{"id":17,"title":"Docker and kubectl runtime commands","level":"INTER","cat":"Containers","purpose":"Build, run, inspect, and deploy an automation container using versioned images.","config":["# build and test locally","docker build -t netops-webhook:1.0.0 .","docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 --env-file .env netops-webhook:1.0.0","docker ps","docker logs --tail 50 $(docker ps -q --filter ancestor=netops-webhook:1.0.0)","# push a versioned image to the approved registry","docker tag netops-webhook:1.0.0 registry.example.net/netops/webhook:1.0.0","docker push registry.example.net/netops/webhook:1.0.0","# deploy an immutable digest in Kubernetes","kubectl apply -f webhook-deployment.yaml","kubectl rollout status deployment/netops-webhook -n automation","kubectl get pods -n automation","kubectl logs deployment/netops-webhook -n automation"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: Docker validates the image locally while kubectl applies and observes the declared Kubernetes workload. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: using only latest makes it impossible to prove which image version ran. EXAM ANGLE: use rollout status and workload logs to verify deployment rather than treating a successful apply as proof of service health."},{"id":18,"title":"GitLab CI validation and deployment pipeline","level":"INTER","cat":"CI/CD","purpose":"Define a GitLab pipeline that validates Terraform and Ansible before a manually approved production apply.","config":["# .gitlab-ci.yml","stages: [validate, test, deploy]","validate:"," stage: validate"," script:"," - terraform fmt -check -recursive"," - terraform validate"," - ansible-lint playbooks/","test_lab:"," stage: test"," script:"," - ansible-playbook -i inventory/lab.yml playbooks/site.yml --check","deploy_prod:"," stage: deploy"," when: manual"," environment: production"," script:"," - terraform apply -auto-approve network.tfplan"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: validation and lab check mode execute before production deployment, and the deployment job requires an explicit manual action. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: running apply in the validate stage blends testing with production mutation and defeats the promotion gate. EXAM ANGLE: protected environments and protected variables should further restrict the deploy job."},{"id":19,"title":"gNMI streaming telemetry subscription","level":"INTER","cat":"Telemetry","purpose":"Subscribe to interface counters with gNMI STREAM mode using the pygnmi client.","config":["# pip install pygnmi","import os","from pygnmi.client import gNMIclient","subscription = {"," 'subscription': [{'path': 'interfaces/interface/state/counters', 'mode': 'sample', 'sample_interval': 10000000000}],"," 'mode': 'stream',"," 'encoding': 'json_ietf',","}","target = (os.environ['GNMI_HOST'], 57400)","with gNMIclient(target=target, username=os.environ['GNMI_USER'], password=os.environ['GNMI_PASSWORD'], insecure=True) as gc:"," for update in gc.subscribe2(subscribe=subscription):"," print(update)"," if 'sync_response' in update:"," print('initial telemetry sync complete')"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: the subscription selects a modeled counters path, uses STREAM mode, and prints updates until the client exits. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: a one-time GET cannot provide continuous model-driven telemetry. EXAM ANGLE: use capabilities discovery and trusted TLS configuration before relying on a production gNMI target."},{"id":20,"title":"Flask webhook receiver with HMAC verification","level":"ADV","cat":"Webhooks","purpose":"Receive a signed controller webhook, reject invalid signatures, and enqueue only authenticated events.","config":["# pip install flask","import hashlib, hmac, os","from flask import Flask, abort, request","app = Flask(__name__)","secret = os.environ['WEBHOOK_SECRET'].encode()","@app.post('/webhook')","def webhook():"," raw = request.get_data()"," expected = hmac.new(secret, raw, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()"," received = request.headers.get('X-Signature-256', '').removeprefix('sha256=')"," if not hmac.compare_digest(expected, received):"," abort(401)"," event = request.get_json(force=True)"," print('accepted event', event.get('id'))"," return {'accepted': True}, 202","if __name__ == '__main__':"," app.run(host='0.0.0.0', port=8080)"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: HMAC is calculated over the raw request body and compare_digest avoids timing-sensitive comparison behavior. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: accepting JSON before verification lets an unauthenticated sender trigger the workflow. EXAM ANGLE: return 202 after durable queueing for asynchronous work; do not perform a long remediation inside the webhook request."},{"id":21,"title":"Catalyst Center asynchronous task poller","level":"ADV","cat":"Catalyst Center API","purpose":"Poll a Catalyst Center task endpoint until an asynchronous workflow reports success or failure.","config":["# pip install requests","import os, time, requests","base = os.environ['CATALYST_CENTER_URL'].rstrip('/')","headers = {'X-Auth-Token': os.environ['CATALYST_CENTER_TOKEN']}","task_id = os.environ['CATALYST_CENTER_TASK_ID']","for attempt in range(30):"," reply = requests.get(base + '/dna/intent/api/v1/task/' + task_id, headers=headers, verify=False, timeout=20)"," reply.raise_for_status()"," task = reply.json()['response']"," if task.get('isError') is True:"," raise RuntimeError(task.get('failureReason', 'task failed'))"," if task.get('progress') == 'Completed':"," print('task completed', task_id)"," break"," time.sleep(5)","else:"," raise TimeoutError('task did not complete before deadline')"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: the poller has a bounded attempt count, checks explicit error state, and waits for the asynchronous task to complete. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: assuming the initial API response means the controller has finished ignores task-based API behavior. EXAM ANGLE: automation must follow task URLs or IDs when a controller returns an asynchronous acceptance response."},{"id":22,"title":"Guarded event remediation client","level":"ADV","cat":"Event Automation","purpose":"Perform an idempotent interface enable only after current state proves the action is required.","config":["# pip install requests","import os, requests","base = os.environ['CONTROLLER_URL'].rstrip('/')","headers = {'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + os.environ['CONTROLLER_TOKEN']}","device_id = os.environ['DEVICE_ID']","interface = 'GigabitEthernet1'","url = base + '/api/v1/devices/' + device_id + '/interfaces/' + interface","state = requests.get(url, headers=headers, timeout=20)","state.raise_for_status()","if state.json()['adminStatus'] == 'down':"," change = requests.patch(url, headers=headers, json={'adminStatus': 'up'}, timeout=20)"," change.raise_for_status()"," print('remediation applied')","else:"," print('no-op: desired state already present')","# always verify post-change telemetry and write an audit event"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: the precheck makes the action idempotent by changing only interfaces whose state differs from desired state. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: blindly PATCHing every alert creates configuration churn and can hide an upstream fault. EXAM ANGLE: webhook-triggered remediation should authenticate, precheck, change, verify, and audit."},{"id":23,"title":"Kubernetes deployment for webhook automation","level":"ADV","cat":"Kubernetes","purpose":"Deploy a least-privilege webhook receiver with a non-root security context and health probes.","config":["# webhook-deployment.yaml","apiVersion: apps/v1","kind: Deployment","metadata: {name: netops-webhook, namespace: automation}","spec:"," replicas: 2"," selector: {matchLabels: {app: netops-webhook}}"," template:"," metadata: {labels: {app: netops-webhook}}"," spec:"," containers:"," - name: receiver"," image: registry.example.net/netops/webhook@sha256:replace-with-approved-digest"," ports: [{containerPort: 8080}]"," securityContext: {runAsNonRoot: true, allowPrivilegeEscalation: false}"," readinessProbe: {httpGet: {path: /health, port: 8080}}"," livenessProbe: {httpGet: {path: /health, port: 8080}}"," envFrom: [{secretRef: {name: netops-webhook-secret}}]"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: the Deployment declares replicas, immutable image identity, non-root execution, health probes, and runtime secret injection. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: embedding a password in YAML or using a mutable image tag weakens both security and deployment evidence. EXAM ANGLE: Kubernetes controllers reconcile the declared Pod template and replica count continuously."},{"id":24,"title":"AI tool allowlist and human approval gate","level":"ADV","cat":"AI in Automation","purpose":"Constrain an AI-assisted operations service to approved read tools and require named approval for write tools.","config":["# ai_tool_gate.py","READ_TOOLS = {'get_interface', 'get_bgp_summary', 'get_recent_alerts'}","WRITE_TOOLS = {'apply_interface_description', 'deploy_bgp_policy'}","def authorize(tool, approver=None):"," if tool in READ_TOOLS:"," return True"," if tool in WRITE_TOOLS and approver:"," return True"," return False","proposal = {'tool': 'deploy_bgp_policy', 'args': {'policy': 'edge-inbound'}}","approver = None","# set approver only after the change record is reviewed","if not authorize(proposal['tool'], approver):"," raise PermissionError('tool call needs approved human authorization')","print('authorized tool call', proposal['tool'])","# log prompt, evidence, approver, tool arguments, and verification result"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: the allowlist separates read-only capability from state-changing tools and requires an explicit approver for writes. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: prompt text asking the model to be careful does not technically prevent a sensitive tool call. EXAM ANGLE: AI-assisted automation needs grounding, least privilege, human gates, and auditable tool execution."}]; window.SCRIPT_SAMPLES_CBRCOR = [{"id":1,"title":"Splunk beaconing hunt","level":"CORE","cat":"SIEM hunting","purpose":"Find rare destinations contacted at unusually regular intervals.","config":["index=network sourcetype=proxy","| eval dest=coalesce(dest_domain,dest_ip)","| bin _time span=5m","| stats count as connections by src_ip,dest,_time","| stats count as intervals values(_time) as windows by src_ip,dest","| where intervals >= 6","| sort - intervals","| table src_ip dest intervals connections windows"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: Five-minute bins reveal repeated outbound connections that can indicate command-and-control beaconing. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Searching only for port 443 produces excessive normal web traffic and misses timing behavior. EXAM ANGLE: Beaconing analytics combine periodicity, rarity, and destination context rather than a single port."},{"id":2,"title":"Splunk lateral movement hunt","level":"CORE","cat":"SIEM hunting","purpose":"Find administrative-share access followed by remote service creation.","config":["index=windows (EventCode=5140 OR EventCode=7045)","| eval host=coalesce(dest_host,ComputerName)","| eval share=coalesce(ShareName,\"-\")","| stats values(EventCode) as events values(share) as shares values(ServiceName) as services by src_ip,host,user","| where mvcount(events) >= 2","| search shares=\"*ADMIN$*\" OR shares=\"*C$*\"","| sort host user","| table src_ip host user shares services events"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: The analytic correlates file-share access and a service-install artifact against the same target context. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: A service-install event alone also occurs in legitimate software deployment and lacks the preceding access clue. EXAM ANGLE: Remote Services often leaves both SMB-share and service-control telemetry."},{"id":3,"title":"Splunk brute-force triage","level":"CORE","cat":"SIEM hunting","purpose":"Identify repeated failed logons followed by a success from the same source.","config":["index=windows (EventCode=4624 OR EventCode=4625)","| eval result=if(EventCode=4625,\"fail\",\"success\")","| stats count(eval(result=\"fail\")) as fails count(eval(result=\"success\")) as successes values(user) as users by src_ip,host","| where fails >= 10 AND successes >= 1","| eval risk=case(fails>=50,\"high\",fails>=20,\"medium\",true(),\"review\")","| sort - fails","| table src_ip host users fails successes risk","| rename src_ip as source_ip"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: The query looks for a transition from repeated failures to success, which is more meaningful than failures alone. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: A threshold without source and target grouping blends unrelated users and systems. EXAM ANGLE: Authentication detections require event semantics and aggregation keys."},{"id":4,"title":"Splunk suspicious PowerShell","level":"CORE","cat":"Detection engineering","purpose":"Find encoded PowerShell executions from Office applications.","config":["index=endpoint sourcetype=Sysmon EventCode=1","| eval parent=lower(ParentImage)","| eval cmd=lower(CommandLine)","| search parent=\"*winword.exe\" OR parent=\"*excel.exe\" OR parent=\"*outlook.exe\"","| search cmd=\"*powershell*\"","| search cmd=\"*-enc*\" OR cmd=\"*encodedcommand*\"","| table _time host user ParentImage Image CommandLine Hashes","| sort - _time"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: Office spawning encoded PowerShell is an unusual and high-signal process relationship. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Searching for PowerShell alone produces many administrative false positives. EXAM ANGLE: Parent-child context is a durable ATT&CK-aligned detection feature."},{"id":5,"title":"Splunk impossible-travel context","level":"CORE","cat":"Cloud monitoring","purpose":"Flag rapid identity sign-ins from different countries for the same user.","config":["index=cloud sourcetype=azure:aad:signin","| eval user=lower(userPrincipalName)","| sort 0 user _time","| streamstats current=f window=1 last(country) as prior_country last(_time) as prior_time by user","| eval minutes=round((_time-prior_time)/60,1)","| where country!=prior_country AND minutes<60","| table _time user prior_country country minutes ipAddress appDisplayName","| sort - _time"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: The query compares each sign-in with the preceding one for the same user and keeps short cross-country transitions. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Country change by itself is normal for travelers and VPN egress. EXAM ANGLE: Identity analytics need corroboration such as VPN, device, and MFA context before containment."},{"id":6,"title":"Python IOC enrichment client","level":"CORE","cat":"Automation","purpose":"Query an internal IOC enrichment API and produce a compact analyst summary.","config":["import os","import requests","ioc = \"198.51.100.23\"","base = os.environ[\"IOC_API_URL\"].rstrip(\"/\")","token = os.environ[\"IOC_API_TOKEN\"]","headers = {\"Authorization\": f\"Bearer {token}\", \"Accept\": \"application/json\"}","response = requests.get(f\"{base}/v1/iocs/{ioc}\", headers=headers, timeout=15)","response.raise_for_status()","data = response.json()","print({\"ioc\": ioc, \"verdict\": data.get(\"verdict\"), \"score\": data.get(\"score\")})"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: The client reads credentials from environment variables, sets a timeout, and fails closed on HTTP errors. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Embedding a token in source code exposes a reusable secret and omitting timeouts can stall a playbook. EXAM ANGLE: API integrations should validate responses and keep secrets out of code."},{"id":7,"title":"VirusTotal-style hash lookup","level":"CORE","cat":"Automation","purpose":"Retrieve a file hash verdict from a reputation API using a bearer token.","config":["import os","import requests","sha256 = \"0123456789abcdef\" * 4","url = f\"https://reputation.example/api/v3/files/{sha256}\"","headers = {\"x-apikey\": os.environ[\"REPUTATION_API_KEY\"]}","resp = requests.get(url, headers=headers, timeout=20)","if resp.status_code == 404:"," print(\"hash not found\")"," raise SystemExit(0)","resp.raise_for_status()","print(resp.json()[\"data\"][\"attributes\"].get(\"last_analysis_stats\", {}))"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: The request uses a supplied API key, a deterministic hash URL, and explicit handling for an unknown sample. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Treating a 404 as malicious or parsing every response as success creates incorrect case evidence. EXAM ANGLE: Reputation is enrichment, not proof; record the source and lookup time."},{"id":8,"title":"Volatility memory triage","level":"CORE","cat":"Forensics","purpose":"List processes, network connections, and command lines from a Windows memory image.","config":["# Set the evidence image path","export MEM=/evidence/host01.raw","# Identify the image and supported symbols","python3 vol.py -f \"$MEM\" windows.info","# Review active and terminated process artifacts","python3 vol.py -f \"$MEM\" windows.pslist","# Review network objects","python3 vol.py -f \"$MEM\" windows.netscan","# Recover process command lines","python3 vol.py -f \"$MEM\" windows.cmdline","# Preserve console output with the case notes"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: The commands enumerate complementary volatile artifacts without altering the evidence image. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Rebooting the endpoint before collection destroys the memory-resident data these plugins analyze. EXAM ANGLE: Memory triage commonly begins with OS identification, processes, sockets, and command lines."},{"id":9,"title":"Disk imaging and hash verification","level":"CORE","cat":"Forensics","purpose":"Acquire a raw disk image and record SHA-256 integrity values.","config":["# Read source media through an approved write blocker","sudo dd if=/dev/sdb of=/evidence/case-104/disk01.img bs=4M conv=noerror,sync status=progress","# Flush pending output before hashing","sync","# Calculate the acquired image digest","sha256sum /evidence/case-104/disk01.img | tee /evidence/case-104/disk01.img.sha256","# Record source, operator, UTC time, and digest in custody log","date -u +\"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ\"","# Verify a later copy against the recorded digest","sha256sum -c /evidence/case-104/disk01.img.sha256"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: A block-level acquisition plus SHA-256 record supports integrity checking of the acquired copy. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Mounting and browsing the original read-write can change timestamps and filesystem metadata. EXAM ANGLE: Forensics questions emphasize write protection, hashing, documentation, and analysis of copies."},{"id":10,"title":"TCP capture for DNS tunneling review","level":"CORE","cat":"Network forensics","purpose":"Capture DNS traffic from a suspected endpoint for later protocol analysis.","config":["# Capture only DNS traffic involving the suspect host","sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -nn -s 0 -w suspect-dns.pcap"," host 10.20.30.45 and udp port 53","# Summarize queried names and lengths","tshark -r suspect-dns.pcap -Y dns.qry.name"," -T fields -e frame.time -e ip.dst -e dns.qry.name"," -e dns.qry.name.len","# Sort long or highly variable labels during analysis","tshark -r suspect-dns.pcap -Y \"dns.qry.name.len > 45\""],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: A focused full-snap-length capture preserves DNS query content while limiting unrelated data collection. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Capturing only packet counts or filtering on destination port 443 would not reveal DNS label behavior. EXAM ANGLE: DNS tunneling review looks for long, encoded, rare, or periodic query patterns."},{"id":11,"title":"YARA suspicious loader rule","level":"INTER","cat":"Malware analysis","purpose":"Detect a sample family pattern using a string and PE-header condition.","config":["rule Suspicious_Encoded_Loader","{"," meta:"," author = \"SOC\""," purpose = \"triage encoded loader behavior\""," strings:"," $ps = \"powershell -enc\" nocase"," $b64 = \"FromBase64String\" ascii wide"," $mz = { 4D 5A }"," condition:"," $mz at 0 and 1 of ($ps, $b64)","}"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: The rule requires a PE header and at least one behavior-relevant string to reduce accidental text matches. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: A rule that matches only `MZ` is far too broad because most Windows executables begin with it. EXAM ANGLE: YARA combines strings and conditions; validate rules against benign and malicious corpora."},{"id":12,"title":"Sigma remote service creation rule","level":"INTER","cat":"Detection engineering","purpose":"Create a portable detection for suspicious service installation telemetry.","config":["title: Remote Service Creation","id: 4fba8ac1-3f1d-4ff6-a71f-9a7f0a0d9101","status: test","logsource:"," product: windows"," service: system","detection:"," selection:"," EventID: 7045"," condition: selection","level: high"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: Windows System event 7045 is a common service-install signal that detection backends can map from Sigma. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Marking a rule production-ready without testing field mappings and deployment patterns causes unreliable alerting. EXAM ANGLE: Sigma expresses detection logic independently of a target SIEM syntax."},{"id":13,"title":"Regex firewall log parser","level":"INTER","cat":"Log normalization","purpose":"Extract common firewall fields from a key-value traffic log line.","config":["import re","line = \"src=10.1.2.3 dst=198.51.100.8 spt=51544 dpt=443 action=allow\"","pattern = re.compile("," r\"src=(?P\\S+) dst=(?P\\S+) \""," r\"spt=(?P\\d+) dpt=(?P\\d+) \""," r\"action=(?P\\w+)\"",")","match = pattern.search(line)","if not match:"," raise ValueError(\"unparseable firewall record\")","print(match.groupdict())"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: Named groups produce stable fields that a SIEM or enrichment pipeline can normalize. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: A greedy `.*` expression can silently consume delimiters and misassign fields. EXAM ANGLE: Reliable parsing is foundational to correlation and data-model consistency."},{"id":14,"title":"Webhook signature validation","level":"INTER","cat":"SOAR integration","purpose":"Validate an HMAC-signed webhook before processing a security event.","config":["import hashlib","import hmac","import os","from flask import Flask, request, abort","app = Flask(__name__)","@app.post(\"/alert\")","def alert():"," body = request.get_data()"," expected = hmac.new(os.environ[\"WEBHOOK_SECRET\"].encode(), body, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()"," if not hmac.compare_digest(expected, request.headers.get(\"X-Signature\", \"\")):"," abort(401)"," return {\"accepted\": True}, 202"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: HMAC verification proves that the payload was signed by a party holding the shared secret and has not changed in transit. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Trusting only a source IP or a user-controlled JSON field allows forged alert submissions. EXAM ANGLE: Webhook integrations require authenticity validation before any automated action."},{"id":15,"title":"Timeline building from CSV evidence","level":"INTER","cat":"Forensics","purpose":"Normalize timestamps from several CSV exports into an ordered investigation timeline.","config":["import csv","from datetime import datetime, timezone","events = []","with open(\"events.csv\", newline=\"\") as fh:"," for row in csv.DictReader(fh):"," ts = datetime.fromisoformat(row[\"timestamp\"].replace(\"Z\", \"+00:00\"))"," events.append((ts.astimezone(timezone.utc), row[\"source\"], row[\"event\"]))","for ts, source, event in sorted(events):"," print(ts.isoformat(), source, event, sep=\" | \")","# Preserve the source filename and timezone conversion in case notes"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: Converting timestamps to UTC before sorting prevents a misleading sequence across sources with different time zones. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Sorting raw timestamp strings from mixed time zones can place events in the wrong order. EXAM ANGLE: Timeline reliability depends on time source, zone, precision, and provenance."},{"id":16,"title":"Splunk rare process-parent hunt","level":"INTER","cat":"Detection engineering","purpose":"Find uncommon parent-child process relationships that may require review.","config":["index=endpoint sourcetype=Sysmon EventCode=1","| eval pair=lower(ParentImage).\" -> \".lower(Image)","| stats count as executions dc(host) as hosts values(CommandLine) as commands by pair","| eventstats sum(executions) as total","| eval rate=round(executions/total,6)","| where executions <= 3 AND hosts <= 2","| sort executions","| table pair executions hosts rate commands"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: Rare parent-child pairs are a behavioral starting point for hunting and can surface new abuse paths. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Automatically blocking every rare pair would disrupt legitimate installers, updaters, and line-of-business tools. EXAM ANGLE: Rarity is a prioritization feature, not a standalone malicious verdict."},{"id":17,"title":"TLS certificate triage with tshark","level":"INTER","cat":"Network forensics","purpose":"Extract SNI and certificate fields from a packet capture for destination analysis.","config":["# Read TLS ClientHello and certificate metadata","tshark -r traffic.pcap"," -Y \"tls.handshake.type == 1 or tls.handshake.type == 11\""," -T fields"," -e frame.time -e ip.src -e ip.dst"," -e tls.handshake.extensions_server_name"," -e x509sat.uTF8String"," -E header=y -E separator=,","# Compare rare SNI names to proxy and DNS telemetry"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: TLS handshake metadata can provide destination context even when application payloads are encrypted. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Assuming that every encrypted connection is malicious ignores normal modern traffic. EXAM ANGLE: Encrypted-traffic investigations correlate SNI, certificate, DNS, timing, and endpoint process context."},{"id":18,"title":"Python API rate-limit retry","level":"INTER","cat":"Automation","purpose":"Call an enrichment API with bounded exponential backoff for rate limits.","config":["import time","import requests","url = \"https://api.example/v1/reputation/203.0.113.9\"","for attempt in range(4):"," response = requests.get(url, timeout=15)"," if response.status_code != 429:"," response.raise_for_status()"," print(response.json())"," break"," delay = int(response.headers.get(\"Retry-After\", 2 ** attempt))"," time.sleep(delay)","else:"," raise RuntimeError(\"enrichment API remained rate limited\")"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: The loop honors an explicit retry delay when available and stops after a bounded number of attempts. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: An unbounded tight retry loop worsens the rate limit and can stall a SOAR worker. EXAM ANGLE: Production automation must handle 429 responses and avoid retry storms."},{"id":19,"title":"Threat-intel STIX bundle extraction","level":"INTER","cat":"Threat intelligence","purpose":"Read indicator patterns from a STIX 2 bundle for controlled enrichment.","config":["import json","with open(\"intel-bundle.json\") as fh:"," bundle = json.load(fh)","for obj in bundle.get(\"objects\", []):"," if obj.get(\"type\") != \"indicator\":"," continue"," print({"," \"id\": obj.get(\"id\"),"," \"pattern\": obj.get(\"pattern\"),"," \"confidence\": obj.get(\"confidence\"),"," \"valid_until\": obj.get(\"valid_until\"),"," })"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: The code selects STIX indicator objects and retains confidence and validity metadata alongside the pattern. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Ingesting every object as a blockable IOC ignores object types, confidence, expiry, and local relevance. EXAM ANGLE: Threat intelligence must be assessed and contextualized before enforcement."},{"id":20,"title":"Baseline log-source health query","level":"ADV","cat":"SIEM engineering","purpose":"Detect security log sources that stopped reporting within the expected window.","config":["index=_internal source=*metrics.log group=per_sourcetype_thruput","| eval source_key=series","| stats max(_time) as last_seen sum(kb) as kb by source_key","| eval minutes_silent=round((now()-last_seen)/60,1)","| where minutes_silent > 30","| eval status=if(minutes_silent>120,\"critical\",\"warning\")","| convert ctime(last_seen)","| sort - minutes_silent","| table source_key last_seen minutes_silent kb status"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: Detection quality depends on telemetry availability, so the query measures the last observed throughput by source key. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Reviewing only alert volume can miss a silent collector that produces no alerts at all. EXAM ANGLE: Data-source health is a first-class SOC control and should have its own detection and escalation path."},{"id":21,"title":"Volatility injected-code review","level":"ADV","cat":"Forensics","purpose":"Identify processes with suspicious memory regions and dump candidates for offline review.","config":["# Review VAD protections for executable writable regions","python3 vol.py -f /evidence/host01.raw windows.malfind","# Save suspicious process memory where supported","python3 vol.py -f /evidence/host01.raw windows.malfind --dump","# Cross-check the process tree","python3 vol.py -f /evidence/host01.raw windows.pstree","# Compare network activity by PID","python3 vol.py -f /evidence/host01.raw windows.netscan","# Hash exported artifacts before submitting to a sandbox","sha256sum *.dmp","# Record the plugin version and symbol set in case notes"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: Malfind-style analysis identifies memory regions with suspicious protections and helps target deeper review. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Treating every writable executable region as malware ignores JIT engines and legitimate software behavior. EXAM ANGLE: Advanced memory analysis correlates injected regions with process lineage, sockets, and code evidence."},{"id":22,"title":"Sigma credential-dumping behavior rule","level":"ADV","cat":"Detection engineering","purpose":"Detect a process attempting to access the LSASS process with suspicious access rights.","config":["title: Suspicious LSASS Process Access","id: b4c06cc7-5d96-4f80-8a8e-260c98e635c5","status: test","logsource:"," product: windows"," category: process_access","detection:"," target_lsass:"," TargetImage|endswith: \\lsass.exe"," suspicious_access:"," GrantedAccess|contains: \"0x1\""," condition: target_lsass and suspicious_access","level: high"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: The rule uses a target process and access-rights context to identify credential-access behavior. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Alerting on every read of LSASS without access context can generate noise from security tools and legitimate monitoring. EXAM ANGLE: Credential dumping detections need tested backend mappings and allowlists for approved security software."},{"id":23,"title":"SOAR idempotent isolation action","level":"ADV","cat":"Automation","purpose":"Isolate an endpoint only if its current state is not already isolated.","config":["import requests","host_id = \"a1b2c3\"","base = \"https://edr.example/api/v1\"","headers = {\"Authorization\": \"Bearer \" + __import__(\"os\").environ[\"EDR_TOKEN\"]}","current = requests.get(f\"{base}/hosts/{host_id}\", headers=headers, timeout=15)","current.raise_for_status()","if current.json().get(\"network_isolation\"):"," print(\"already isolated; no duplicate action\")","else:"," change = requests.post(f\"{base}/hosts/{host_id}/isolate\", headers=headers, timeout=15)"," change.raise_for_status()"," print(\"isolation requested\", change.status_code)"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: The code reads current endpoint state before changing it, making repeated webhook delivery safe. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Blindly posting an isolate request on every alert can create duplicate actions and ambiguous audit trails. EXAM ANGLE: Idempotency is essential when SOAR systems retry jobs or receive duplicate events."},{"id":24,"title":"Risk-prioritized vulnerability export","level":"ADV","cat":"Risk assessment","purpose":"Prioritize vulnerabilities using severity, exploit status, and asset criticality.","config":["import csv","with open(\"findings.csv\", newline=\"\") as fh:"," findings = list(csv.DictReader(fh))","for f in findings:"," cvss = float(f[\"cvss\"]); criticality = int(f[\"asset_criticality\"])"," exploited = f[\"known_exploited\"].lower() == \"true\""," f[\"priority\"] = cvss * criticality + (30 if exploited else 0)","ranked = sorted(findings, key=lambda x: x[\"priority\"], reverse=True)","for f in ranked[:20]:"," print(f[\"asset\"], f[\"cve\"], f[\"priority\"], f[\"owner\"], sep=\",\")","# Validate ownership and compensating controls before escalation"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: The ranking adds exploit status and asset criticality to CVSS, creating a more operational remediation order. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Sorting only by CVSS can prioritize a harmless lab server above an exploited issue on a critical system. EXAM ANGLE: Risk-based vulnerability management combines technical severity with exposure and business context."}]; window.SCRIPT_SAMPLES_WLCOR = [{"id":1,"title":"Build a reusable corporate WLAN, policy profile, and policy tag","level":"CORE","cat":"9800 profiles","purpose":"Creates an enterprise SSID and maps it to reusable client policy for AP assignment.","config":["! Create the client-facing WLAN profile","wlan CORP 10 CORP"," no shutdown","! Create the policy used after association","wireless profile policy CORP-POLICY"," vlan 110"," no shutdown","! Bind the WLAN and policy profile in a policy tag","wireless tag policy HQ-POLICY-TAG"," wlan CORP policy CORP-POLICY","! Apply HQ-POLICY-TAG through AP tag assignment"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: The WLAN profile defines the SSID while the policy profile defines the client treatment, and the policy tag binds the two. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Configuring only the WLAN leaves no policy mapping at the AP. EXAM ANGLE: Distinguish WLAN, policy profile, policy tag, site tag, and RF tag responsibilities."},{"id":2,"title":"Assign policy, site, and RF tags to an AP","level":"CORE","cat":"AP provisioning","purpose":"Applies the reusable tag set to a specific Catalyst AP after it has joined.","config":["! Use the AP Ethernet MAC address shown by show ap summary","ap 1234.5678.90ab"," policy-tag HQ-POLICY-TAG"," site-tag HQ-SITE-TAG"," rf-tag HQ-RF-TAG","! Verify the intended assignment","end","show ap tag summary","show ap name AP-HQ-01 tag detail"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: The AP receives a policy tag, site tag, and RF tag that select the appropriate profiles. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Applying a policy profile directly to the AP bypasses the Catalyst 9800 tag model. EXAM ANGLE: Tags are the attachment point between reusable profiles and APs."},{"id":3,"title":"Configure a WPA3-Personal SAE SSID","level":"CORE","cat":"WPA3","purpose":"Enables a WPA3-Personal SSID with SAE and protected management frames.","config":["! WPA3-Personal WLAN","wlan STAFF-WPA3 20 STAFF-WPA3"," security wpa psk set-key ascii 0 ChangeMe-Staff-2026"," security wpa akm sae"," security wpa wpa3"," security pmf mandatory"," no shutdown","! Map STAFF-WPA3 to an existing policy profile","wireless tag policy HQ-POLICY-TAG"," wlan STAFF-WPA3 policy CORP-POLICY"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: SAE provides WPA3-Personal authentication and PMF protects management traffic as required by WPA3. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Leaving only WPA2-PSK configured does not enable SAE, and optional PMF is not the WPA3 baseline. EXAM ANGLE: Know that WPA3-Personal uses SAE rather than a legacy PSK handshake."},{"id":4,"title":"Configure WPA3-Enterprise with 802.1X","level":"CORE","cat":"802.1X","purpose":"Creates an enterprise WLAN that authenticates users through an existing RADIUS method list.","config":["! AAA method list must reference reachable RADIUS servers","aaa authentication dot1x DOT1X-ISE group ISE-RADIUS","! Enterprise WLAN","wlan CORP-EAP 21 CORP-EAP"," security wpa akm dot1x"," security wpa wpa2 ciphers aes"," security wpa wpa3"," security pmf mandatory"," security dot1x authentication-list DOT1X-ISE"," no shutdown"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: The WLAN selects 802.1X AKM and points EAP authentication to the DOT1X-ISE method list. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: A PSK AKM bypasses RADIUS EAP entirely, while a missing authentication list leaves no enterprise AAA path. EXAM ANGLE: Authentication method list selection is configured at the WLAN security layer."},{"id":5,"title":"Prepare an iPSK WLAN with ISE authorization","level":"CORE","cat":"iPSK","purpose":"Creates the controller-side WLAN behavior needed when ISE supplies individual PSK policy and authorization.","config":["! ISE owns the individual PSK lifecycle and identity policy","aaa authorization network ISE-AUTHZ group ISE-RADIUS","wlan IOT-IPSK 30 IOT-IPSK"," security wpa akm psk"," security wpa wpa2 ciphers aes"," security wpa psk set-key ascii 0 Bootstrap-Only-DoNotUse"," aaa-override"," no shutdown","! Use ISE policy to return the per-device authorization result"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: The WLAN uses PSK security while AAA override permits per-device authorization from ISE, where iPSK policy is managed. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: A single static PSK with no AAA integration cannot differentiate device policy. EXAM ANGLE: iPSK improves accountability and segmentation but still needs a compatible identity-policy design."},{"id":6,"title":"Configure guest CWA redirect with ISE","level":"CORE","cat":"Guest access","purpose":"Builds an open guest WLAN that redirects a restricted pre-authenticated session to an ISE portal.","config":["! Pre-auth ACL must permit DNS and the portal while blocking general access","ip access-list extended GUEST-PREAUTH"," permit udp any any eq domain"," permit tcp any host 192.0.2.50 eq 8443"," deny ip any any","! Guest WLAN","wlan GUEST-CWA 40 GUEST-CWA"," security web-auth"," security web-auth parameter-map ISE-CWA"," no shutdown","! Use ISE RADIUS policy to return post-login dACL or VLAN"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: Web authentication redirects the guest session while the pre-auth ACL allows only onboarding dependencies. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Permitting all traffic before portal completion defeats captive access control. EXAM ANGLE: CWA has separate pre-auth and post-auth authorization states."},{"id":7,"title":"Create a FlexConnect profile for local switching","level":"CORE","cat":"FlexConnect","purpose":"Maps a branch WLAN to a local VLAN and defines the native VLAN for a FlexConnect AP.","config":["! Local VLANs must also be allowed on the AP switchport trunk","wireless profile flex BRANCH-FLEX"," native-vlan-id 10"," vlan-name CORP-VLAN 110"," vlan-name GUEST-VLAN 120"," no shutdown","! Attach the Flex profile through the branch site tag","wireless tag site BRANCH-SITE-TAG"," flex-profile BRANCH-FLEX"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: The Flex profile provides local VLAN mappings and the site tag associates that profile with branch APs. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: A wired trunk alone does not map a WLAN to a local VLAN. EXAM ANGLE: FlexConnect can locally switch data while retaining controller CAPWAP control."},{"id":8,"title":"Create a 5 GHz RF profile with controlled width","level":"CORE","cat":"RF profiles","purpose":"Sets a 5 GHz RF profile with a bounded power range and a 40 MHz channel policy.","config":["! Use a named RF profile rather than changing global defaults","ap dot11 5ghz rf-profile HQ-5G-RF"," description HQ capacity profile"," tx-power min 8 max 17"," channel dca chan-width 40"," channel dca interval 600"," no shutdown","! Associate HQ-5G-RF with an RF tag","wireless tag rf HQ-RF-TAG"," 5ghz-rf-policy HQ-5G-RF"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: The RF profile constrains TPC and DCA behavior and the RF tag distributes that profile to APs. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Setting maximum power without a minimum permits undesirable cell-size variation. EXAM ANGLE: Channel width is an RF reuse decision, not a universal throughput setting."},{"id":9,"title":"Enable 5 GHz band select bias","level":"CORE","cat":"Client steering","purpose":"Biases dual-band capable clients toward 5 GHz where coverage supports it.","config":["! Apply after confirming 5 GHz coverage is adequate","ap dot11 5ghz"," band-select","! Keep 2.4 GHz available for clients that need it","ap dot11 24ghz"," no shutdown","! Verify AP radio operational state","end","show ap dot11 5ghz summary","show wireless stats client detail"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: Band select delays or biases selected dual-band probe behavior to encourage 5 GHz association. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Disabling 2.4 GHz is not a substitute when legacy or IoT clients require it. EXAM ANGLE: Steering influences association but the client ultimately selects its band and AP."},{"id":10,"title":"Enable CleanAir spectrum intelligence","level":"CORE","cat":"CleanAir","purpose":"Enables CleanAir monitoring on 5 GHz radios for non-Wi-Fi interferer visibility.","config":["! CleanAir is an RF monitoring feature, not an authentication feature","ap dot11 5ghz"," cleanair","! Retain normal radio service"," no shutdown","end","! Verify interferer and radio information after APs report","show ap dot11 5ghz cleanair air-quality summary","show ap dot11 5ghz cleanair interference summary","show wireless stats ap history"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: CleanAir-class capable radios report non-802.11 interference information for troubleshooting and RRM context. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: A packet capture alone may not identify microwave or analog interferer signatures. EXAM ANGLE: CleanAir evidence is distinct from Wi-Fi co-channel contention."},{"id":11,"title":"Build a resilient RADIUS server group","level":"INTER","cat":"AAA/RADIUS","purpose":"Defines two ISE RADIUS servers and associates them with the enterprise 802.1X method list.","config":["! Define individual RADIUS servers","radius server ISE-PSN1"," address ipv4 192.0.2.51 auth-port 1812 acct-port 1813"," key 0 Replace-With-Shared-Secret","radius server ISE-PSN2"," address ipv4 192.0.2.52 auth-port 1812 acct-port 1813"," key 0 Replace-With-Shared-Secret","aaa group server radius ISE-RADIUS"," server name ISE-PSN1"," server name ISE-PSN2","aaa authentication dot1x DOT1X-ISE group ISE-RADIUS"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: The named server group provides redundant RADIUS targets and the method list selects that group for 802.1X. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Defining servers without adding them to the group does not make them eligible through the method list. EXAM ANGLE: Separate server definitions, server groups, authentication, and authorization method lists."},{"id":12,"title":"Build a per-site tag bundle","level":"INTER","cat":"Tags and profiles","purpose":"Creates a site-specific policy, site, and RF tag bundle for a branch with a different VLAN and RF design.","config":["! Branch policy profile uses its local client VLAN","wireless profile policy BRANCH-CORP-POLICY"," vlan 210"," no shutdown","wireless tag policy BRANCH-POLICY-TAG"," wlan CORP policy BRANCH-CORP-POLICY","wireless tag site BRANCH-SITE-TAG"," ap-join-profile default-ap-profile"," flex-profile BRANCH-FLEX","wireless tag rf BRANCH-RF-TAG"," 5ghz-rf-policy HQ-5G-RF"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: The three tags let a branch reuse the corporate SSID while assigning local VLAN, AP join/Flex, and RF behavior. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Reusing the HQ policy tag would place branch clients in the HQ VLAN policy. EXAM ANGLE: Tags provide scalable per-site variation without cloning every WLAN."},{"id":13,"title":"Configure a mobility group peer","level":"INTER","cat":"Mobility","purpose":"Adds a peer controller to a common mobility group for inter-controller roaming.","config":["! Use the peer controller MAC and management address","wireless mobility group member mac-address aaaa.bbbb.cccc ip-address 192.0.2.12 group CAMPUS-MOBILITY","! Verify local mobility membership and reachability","end","show wireless mobility summary","show wireless mobility group members","show wireless mobility statistics","! Ensure both controllers use compatible mobility design and group name"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: Mobility peers exchange the context needed for compatible inter-controller roaming. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Matching an SSID alone does not establish a mobility relationship. EXAM ANGLE: Controller mobility grouping and client IP subnet are separate parts of roaming design."},{"id":14,"title":"Configure an HA SSO redundancy baseline","level":"INTER","cat":"High availability","purpose":"Enables Stateful Switchover mode and verifies redundancy state on a Catalyst 9800 pair.","config":["! Complete chassis, RP, and management addressing prerequisites first","redundancy"," mode sso"," exit","! Save the intended redundancy mode","end","write memory","show redundancy states","show redundancy clients","show wireless management interface","show wireless stats ap summary"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: Redundancy SSO enables stateful active/standby operation after the pair prerequisites are in place. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: A standalone redundancy mode or missing peer connectivity cannot provide hot-standby takeover. EXAM ANGLE: SSO minimizes disruption; it is not an active-active load-sharing model."},{"id":15,"title":"Configure an inter-controller guest mobility anchor","level":"INTER","cat":"Guest mobility","purpose":"Defines a mobility anchor peer used to centralize guest traffic toward a DMZ controller.","config":["! Add the guest-anchor controller as a mobility peer first","wireless mobility group member mac-address dddd.eeee.ffff ip-address 192.0.2.60 group CAMPUS-MOBILITY","! WLAN policy points guest service toward the anchor design","wireless profile policy GUEST-ANCHOR-POLICY"," vlan 120"," central switching"," no shutdown","! Verify mobility control-plane state before directing guest clients","end","show wireless mobility summary"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: Guest anchoring centralizes traffic toward the controller and security zone designed for internet-only access. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: A local VLAN assignment at every site can bypass the intended DMZ boundary. EXAM ANGLE: Central switching and mobility anchoring are common guest-segmentation design tools."},{"id":16,"title":"Tune RRM DCA and TPC for dense 5 GHz cells","level":"INTER","cat":"RRM","purpose":"Sets bounded channel and power behavior suitable for a dense indoor 5 GHz deployment.","config":["! Tune after survey and baseline validation","ap dot11 5ghz rf-profile DENSE-5G-RF"," channel dca chan-width 20"," channel dca interval 600"," tx-power min 5 max 14"," coverage data rssi threshold -67"," coverage voice rssi threshold -67"," no shutdown","wireless tag rf DENSE-RF-TAG"," 5ghz-rf-policy DENSE-5G-RF"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: Narrower channels and a constrained power range improve reuse control in dense cells, while coverage thresholds define a design target. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Maximum power and 80 MHz everywhere can create large cells and excessive co-channel contention. EXAM ANGLE: RRM is guided by RF profiles, not by arbitrary maximum values."},{"id":17,"title":"Enable FT and assisted roaming on an enterprise WLAN","level":"INTER","cat":"Roaming","purpose":"Enables 802.11r Fast Transition with 802.11k and 802.11v assistance for a validated client population.","config":["! Validate client compatibility before production rollout","wlan CORP-EAP 21 CORP-EAP"," security ft"," security ft over-the-air"," dot11k neighbor-list"," dot11v bss-transition"," no shutdown","! Verify client capability and roam events after change","end","show wireless client mac-address 1234.5678.90ab detail"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: FT shortens the authentication exchange while k supplies neighbor information and v can suggest a BSS transition. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Enabling FT does not repair weak overlap, and k/v do not force the client to roam. EXAM ANGLE: Treat r, k, and v as complementary mechanisms with different roles."},{"id":18,"title":"Configure mDNS service discovery policy","level":"INTER","cat":"mDNS/Bonjour","purpose":"Creates a scoped Bonjour service policy so wireless clients can discover approved local services.","config":["! Define only the service types users require","wireless profile mdns MDNS-PRINTING"," service-type _ipp._tcp.local"," service-type _airplay._tcp.local"," no shutdown","! Associate mDNS profile with client policy","wireless profile policy CORP-POLICY"," mdns-profile MDNS-PRINTING"," no shutdown","! Validate discovery from the intended VLAN and WLAN"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: The mDNS profile allows selected service advertisements to be handled according to wireless policy instead of flooding discovery indiscriminately. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Enabling every service type expands discovery exposure and noise. EXAM ANGLE: Bonjour is multicast-based service discovery that needs deliberate scope across client segments."},{"id":19,"title":"Enable wireless model-driven telemetry export","level":"INTER","cat":"Telemetry","purpose":"Configures an IETF telemetry subscription that streams a selected YANG path to a collector.","config":["! Collector must support the chosen encoding and transport","telemetry ietf subscription 101"," encoding encode-kvgpb"," filter xpath /wireless-ap-oper:ap-global-oper-data"," receiver ip address 192.0.2.200 57500 protocol grpc-tcp"," source-address GigabitEthernet0"," stream yang-push"," update-policy periodic 6000","! Verify the subscription and collector reachability","end","show telemetry ietf subscription 101"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: The subscription identifies a modeled operational data path, encoding, receiver, and update cadence for continuous export. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: A telemetry receiver without a filter or transport definition has no usable data stream. EXAM ANGLE: Streaming telemetry is for observation; NETCONF/RESTCONF are used for modeled configuration interaction."},{"id":20,"title":"Enable NETCONF-YANG management","level":"ADV","cat":"NETCONF/YANG","purpose":"Enables secure NETCONF access for model-driven Catalyst 9800 configuration workflows.","config":["! Use AAA and restricted management access in production","aaa new-model","aaa authentication login NETCONF-LOCAL local","username netops privilege 15 secret 0 Replace-With-Secret","netconf-yang","! NETCONF uses SSH TCP port 830","ip ssh version 2","ip ssh authentication-retries 2","! Verify the service state","end","show netconf-yang status"],"explain":"WHY IT WORKS: netconf-yang enables the YANG-modeled NETCONF service, while AAA and SSH protect management access. WHY A VARIANT FAILS: Enabling SSH by itself does not expose the NETCONF YANG service. EXAM ANGLE: NETCONF commonly edits modeled candidate/running configuration through RPC operations over SSH port 830."},{"id":21,"title":"Enable RESTCONF and issue a sample API read","level":"ADV","cat":"RESTCONF","purpose":"Enables RESTCONF and documents a copy-ready HTTPS GET against a modeled operational resource.","config":["! RESTCONF relies on HTTPS and AAA authorization","aaa new-model","username apiuser privilege 15 secret 0 Replace-With-Secret","ip http secure-server","restconf","! Verify the RESTCONF service","end","show restconf status","!
